#3623. These 10 New Features Are Coming to iOS 27.3

Apple dropped the first developer beta for iOS 27.3 on Tuesday. While this update isn't as large as iOS 27 proper, it's surprisingly feature-filled for a 0.3 update. This is only a beta, so anything could (and likely will) change before Apple officially launches the update. But, as it stands, iOS 27.3 tests 10 new features—including one feature the company trialed in the previous beta.

Technically, anyone with a compatible iPhone can try out iOS 27.3 right now—assuming you enroll your Apple Account in the developer program. But a word of warning: Betas can be temperamental, and could be risky. As such, I'd recommend avoiding the beta until Apple releases the public beta, which comes after a bit more testing to iron out larger issues. Either way, make sure to make a full backup of your iPhone to a Mac or PC first, as issues with the beta could result in permanent data loss.

With watchOS 27, Apple released "Audio Intelligence," a new set of features for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. Audio Intelligence uses the watches' new S11 chip, along with on-device AI and cloud-based AI, to run new features, like Sound Recognition and Shazam (music recognition).

With iOS 27.3, however, the company is now officially testing the other two Audio Intelligence features it originally announced with watchOS 27. First, there's Live Rewind: By double-clicking the watch crown, you can pull up a transcript of the last 15 seconds of a conversation. Siri Recap, on the other hand, displays summaries of conversations you had that day, in case you need a refresher on any chats you might have otherwise forgotten about,

The company generated some controversy when it first announced these two Audio Intelligence features, since, on the surface, it sounds like these new Apple Watches are essentially spying on people all day long. According to Apple, however, that isn't really the case. The company says Audio Intelligence is private, and never records or stores any audio. No speakers are ever identified, and text results (both transcripts and summaries) are deleted automatically after a set period of time unless the user saves them to the Siri app. You can read more about how Audio Intelligence works here.

Despite their claims, I'm sure there will still be strong feelings surrounding these Audio Intelligence features. We'll have to see whether Apple can prove Live Rewind and Siri Recap aren't all that creepy throughout the iOS 27.3 beta process.

iOS 27.3 also introduces app actions for Siri AI. Apple is testing new abilities for Siri AI, including organizing files, planning events, or adding photos to albums. You could ask Siri to organize your Downloads folder, or delete files that haven't been opened in more than a year. You could ask Siri to find a coffee shop you went to last week, or to save an article to your Reading List in Safari. You could ask Siri to check your calendar and set up a time for an event based on when you're free. You can even ask the assistant to schedule, edit, or unsend messages.

For example, you could ask Siri AI to help you plan a trip with your friends. You could ask the AI to put together a themed playlist in Apple Music, schedule a message to a group about an upcoming trip, organize the websites you've been visiting in Safari into a tab group, and, after the trip, ask Siri to move your best photos to your favorites album. These new actions work in the following apps: Calendar, Files, Finder, Journal, Mail, Maps, Messages, Music, Notes, Photos, Preview, Reminders, Safari, Shortcuts, and Weather. Developers can also add Siri AI app actions support to their own apps.

Apple started testing its new Health app with the iOS 27.2 beta, but pulled the redesign before the official release. Now, with iOS 27.3, the new app is back. The new Health app has a health dashboard for the first time, as well as new features like Health Age and movement assessments. It seems to be pulling from some popular competitor services, hopefully, for the better. For more on the new Health app, check out Lifehacker health editor Beth Skwarecki's explainer.

Continuing on the Health track, iOS 27.3 also introduces "Gym Strength." This is a new Fitness+ feature that offers a personalized four-week strength-training plan. You can customize these plans to meet your goals, experience level, and schedule, and they adapt as you progress. You'll get recommendations based on your experience with exercises, reps, and sets, including video demos for exercises. You can access Gym Strength on both iPhone and iPad, and Apple Watches are optional—though you can log your progress with the wearable if you have it.

Vertical tabs have been a favorite among browser aficionados, as they give you more screen real estate in your browser while keeping your tabs off the side. Apple hasn't made the jump—until now. This feature works with iPads running iPadOS 27.3 as well as Macs running macOS 27.3.

Another new Safari feature in testing is "Adaptive Dark Mode." This feature forces websites into a dark theme, if they don't have a native theme of their own. There are third-party apps that can do this, but this is the first time Apple has offered this feature built into Safari.

Apple is also testing new StandBy experiences with iOS 27.3, which were previously only available on the iPhone Duo. When you turn your iPhone sideways while plugged in, you'll find new Analog and Digital Clock faces with new customization options. There's also a new Photos face, with the option to pull images from Shared Albums.

"Reachability" pulls your iPhone's display down towards the bottom of the screen, so you can access items towards the top of the display with one hand. It's a useful feature for those of us with big iPhones, and now, there's no iPhone bigger than the Duo. With iOS 27.3, Apple is testing Reachability for its first foldable phone. It's a bit like the inverse of how Reachability currently works: You can swipe on the left or right side of your Duo's display to shift the other side of the screen towards your current position. If you're holding your Duo in your left hand, a swipe of the left side will pull the right side over to the left, and vice versa.

Apple is also rolling out new languages for Siri AI in iOS 27.3. Now, Apple's smart assistant supports Traditional Chinese, Vietnamese, Turkish, and Norwegian.

If you have an Apple Intelligence-compatible iPad running iPadOS 27.3, you now have access to Siri Mode in Camera. As with iOS, you can open the Camera app on iPadOS to access Siri Mode, and ask Siri about your surroundings.

NCIS Season 24 is off to a hot start, and it's been giving a lot of screen time to Michael Weatherly's Tony DiNozzo, who is currently the new NCIS director. With that storyline dominating, there's been little time to follow other fan-favorite plotlines. This has really gotten me to thinking about how the show cooled off on a potential Jessica Knight and Nicholas Torres romance. CinemaBlend recently had the chance to speak to Knight actress Katrina Law, and I had to ask her about what's going on.

I recently had a chance to speak to Law, and after talking about the recent episode marking the first time she worked with her daughter, I had to know what's going on with Torres. I wondered if fans should just give up on Knight and Wilmer Valderrama's character having a relationship. Here's what she said:

Well, as we know in the show, especially one that's gone on to season 24, nothing's ever dead. I can appreciate Katrina Law's empathy when it comes to Jimmy Palmer. Jimmy and Jessica's relationship was fun while it lasted, but it feels like the door is closed on them ever reconciling and getting back together. Hear me out: Is she just supposed to ignore Torres and the obvious chemistry just because it might hurt her ex's feelings?

Personally, I think fans would say no, and I have a feeling Jimmy would say the same. He's a mature adult, and he's gone through the ups and downs of romance. All that aside, though, we'll have to keep watching NCIS on CBS on Tuesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET to see if there's any momentum between Knight and Torres. In the meantime, there's never a shortage of crimes for the team to solve, and it's been fun to see them navigate that with Tony as their boss.

#3621. The PS5’s New Graphics-Upscaling Trick Is Spreading To More Games

Sony has announced that several more games are getting a Quick Spectral Super Resolution (QSSR) upgrade on PS5. Introduced in September, QSSR is an AI-guided upscaling technology similar to the PS5 Pro's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR), and it originally supported only Marvel's Wolverine and Ghost of Yotei. That lineup is expanding over the next couple of weeks to include games like Control Resonant, Marvel's Spider-Man 2, Arc Raiders, The Finals, No Man's Sky, and Hell Let Loose: Vietnam.

While it's not quite as good as PSSR on the PS5 Pro, QSSR still does a noticeable job of adding detail and clarity without impacting performance. Sony added that since QSSR shares elements with PSSR, it makes games that support the PS5 Pro upscaling tech a "natural" fit for an upgrade on regular PS5 consoles.

Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is a good example, given Insomniac Games' familiarity with PSSR. The QSSR update is now available for the game, and Insomniac's head of technology, Mike Fitzgerald, said it'll apply to both Fidelity and Performance modes. For Control Resonant, Remedy Entertainment senior graphics programmer Erik Jansson said that QSSR will offer noticeable improvements in image stability and fine detail, and the update will be available in December.

While there's no exact date for when Arc Raiders and The Finals will be updated, players can expect "increased sharpness, better environmental clarity and overall visual improvements," according to Embarl Studios technical art director Mikael Linderholm. Hello Games founder Sean Murray said that the No Man's Sky QSSR update will be out in a "few weeks" and will see the game look sharper on PS5 while maintaining "the best possible" frame rate.

Finally, Paul Rustchynsky, game director at Expression Games, said that Hell Let Loose: Vietnam will also look cleaner and sharper on PS5 when the update is eventually available. If you're interested in seeing how different several of the games look with QSSR enabled, you can click the links below to see comparison videos:

  • Control Resonant
  • Arc Raiders
  • No Man's Sky
  • Hell Let Loose: Vietnam

The PS5 turns six years old later this month, and as of November 10, it has surpassed 100 million consoles sold. Ordinarily, all eyes would be on the next PlayStation generation at this point--which Sony says it is working on--and advances like QSSR may squeeze more life out of the PS5 before its successor arrives. Whatever form the next PlayStation takes, don't expect it to be cheap, as the current generation has gotten more expensive since 2020 and the PS6 could cost over $1,000. Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden recently touched on the topic, and he spoke about how true innovation from Sony would come in the form of cheaper hardware, not just better graphics.

#3620. A Look Inside the Scorpion Ball, Princess Grace Kelly’s Scorpio-Themed 40th Birthday Party

Grace Kelly always had a deep passion for astrology. Born on November 12, 1929, she was a Scorpio, and very proud of it. To celebrate her 40th birthday on November 15, 1969, the Princess of Monaco organized a party themed by her astrological sign, resulting in the extravagant Scorpio Ball, held at the Hôtel de l’Hermitage in Monte Carlo. For the occasion, she only invited celebrities who were also Scorpios. Among the 60 or so guests were Swedish actress Hjördis Paulina Genberg, American actor Rock Hudson, and Italian actress Virna Lisi.

Actor Richard Burton was also in attendance, accompanied by his wife Elizabeth Taylor, even though she was born under the sign of Pisces. An exception was made for the actress, who was granted special permission thanks to her husband’s astrological sign—Scorpio, born on November 10. For the occasion, Taylor chose to dazzle, wearing a Cartier diamond necklace with an estimated value of $1 million around her neck—a gift from Burton two weeks earlier. She also wore a spectacular evening cape by Tiziani, made of black velvet and adorned with two rhinestone scorpions on the front and a third on the hood.

Guests were required to adhere to a dress code devised by Kelly, inspired by the colors associated with the sign of Scorpio. Red, black, and white were therefore strongly recommended. The princess, for her part, opted for an off-the-shoulder black velvet dress by Balenciaga from the fall-winter 1967 couture collection. Two ruby brooches set with diamonds—a wedding gift from Prince Rainier III—completed her ensemble.

The decor also reflected the evening’s theme. Red candles, portraits of famous Scorpios, and a lavish cake adorned with golden scorpions set the tone. No detail had been left to chance: The waiters, wearing powdered 18th-century wigs, dressed in velvet suits embroidered with sparkling stars and held silver candelabras adorned with red candles.

Princess Grace was seen on numerous occasions alongside Carroll Righter, an astrologer and Hollywood columnist nicknamed “the astrologer to the stars.” According to People magazine, the princess’s birth chart also revealed a Scorpio ascendant, while her Midheaven was in Leo. In astrology, the Midheaven is associated with career, public image, and reputation. Some attributed her commanding presence and magnetism in the spotlight to this configuration.

Kelly embodied the mysterious aura that her admirers associated with her astrological sign. Unfortunately, that light was extinguished on September 14, 1982, when the Princess of Monaco lost her life in a tragic car accident on the hills above the principality.

#3619. Robert Pattinson Named the Next James Bond After Thorough Search

After a years-long search, Amazon MGM Studios has found its next James Bond in Robert Pattinson.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” Pattinson, 40, said in a statement to Us on Monday, November 16. “I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

When reacting to the news, the actor also gave thanks to director Denis Villeneuve and producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman for giving him the opportunity to play such an iconic character.

Amazon MGM Studios also confirmed the casting by sharing several posts on Instagram with the caption, “Identity Confirmed.”

According to The Hollywood Reporter, the casting process was so secretive that Villeneuve, 59, only informed Pattinson that he got the role on Sunday, November 15. Pascal, 68, is said to have called the runners-up.

“Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey. We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007,” Villeneuve said in a statement to Us. “I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Identity Confirmed pic.twitter.com/FCU5A9c1wk

Pascal added, “James Bond is one of the most beloved, inspiring, iconic and yet enigmatic characters in literature and movies. The legacy of this character is in great hands with Robert Pattinson. His fearlessness as an actor, his self-deprecating wit, and his ability to continually reinvent himself make him the perfect Bond for our times.”

Since breaking out in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire and the Twilight franchise, Pattinson’s acting career has continued to grow and impress fans and movie critics alike.

As the face of DC Studios’ Batman franchise, Pattinson also had a major supporting role in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey and starred in The Drama. He is set to star in Dune: Part Three, which is due out in theaters on December 18. He is also shooting The Batman: Part II, whose production is currently underway in London.

According to Deadline, the process to find the next 007 goes back to the spring, when the studio announced that casting director Nina Gold was joining the project.

While not confirmed, sources told the outlet that Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Nicholas Hoult and Josh O’Connor were some of the actors who also tested for the role.

The Bond casting comes nearly 21 years after Daniel Craig was announced as the suave British secret agent in October 2005. Craig, now 58, starred in Casino Royale, Quantum of Solace, Skyfall and Spectre before his final appearance as 007 in 2021’s No Time to Die.

It's an exciting time to be a Marvel fans, given the release of VisionQuest's finale for those with a Disney+ subscription, as well as the upcoming Marvel movie Avengers: Doomsday being a month and change away from its release. Just last week, Anthony Mackie went viral for seemingly spoiling Paul Bettany's role in Doomsday, but now he's defending those comments. The question is: do we actually believe him?

What we know about Avengers: Doomsday is super limited, so there are countless theories and rumors surrounding the project. The Doomsday cast list includes tons of heroes, but Kevin Feige also confirmed that more surprise heroes would be included. So when Mackie spoke about hanging with Bettany on set, fans thought he might have accidentally revealed a twist. In a clip from The Tonight Show's Instagram, the Hurt Locker actor defended himself to Jimmy Fallon, saying:

So Paul Bettany's my man. That's my homie, right? We hang out all the time. He was shooting VisionQuest next door to where we were shooting Avengers. So, me being me, you know, I steal a golf cart and I pull up. I am a pull up-er. If I hear you're there I'm pulling up.

This potentially offers some much-needed context about Mackie's viral comments about hanging out with Paul Bettany while shooting Doomsday. If the actor is to be believed, he knew that VisionQuest was also shooting at Pinewood Studios in the U.K. at the same time as principal photography for the next Avengers flick. That's how he was able to see his frequent co-star, instead of shooting the crossover event together.

Tom Holland has a reputation for Marvel spoilers, but Mackie's comments about Bettany quickly went viral, especially since VisionQuest featured the return of Elizabeth Olsen's Wanda Maximoff. If The Scarlet Witch will appear in in Doomsday, why not Vision? In the same interview Anthony Mackie went on to say:

I didn't say he was in Doomsday. I said he was next door shooting his show. Just like Tom Holland was next door shooting Spider-Man. He was next door! He wasn't in the movie... I guess.

The "I guess" certainly doesn't inspire confidence. Given Marvel's tight security, actors sometimes have to tell white lies in order to guard the shared universe's spoilers. Case in point: Andrew Garifeld lied about returning as Spider-Man for years ahead of No Way Home's release. As such, we're going to have to wait until the next Avengers movie hits theaters to find out whether or not Mackie was telling the truth about Bettany (and Holland).

All will be revealed when Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters December 18th as part of the 2026 movie release list. Anticipation for The Russo Brothers' blockbuster is at a fever pitch, luckily the wait is nearly over for its debut on the big screen.

But Huang’s recent weeks have not been marked by good times with the besties. First, the Democrats took over Congress, throttling all the goodwill he built with the administration. What’s unknown is the current state of his relationship with his wife, Lori Huang—and their ambitious plans for an arts organization that was set to bear their name. Earlier this year, the Huangs pledged $75 million to Vanderbilt University in order to help transform the soon-to-be-closed legendary San Francisco art school California College of the Arts into part of Vanderbilt’s SF campus. Vanderbilt announced that it planned to name a portion of its SF campus the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design.

Which is now a bit awkward, given the multiple alleged affairs, and the whole Chinese-spy thing. Plus, Huang is no longer affiliated with Nvidia, which teamed up with CCA in 2025 to form the CCA-Nvidia Incubator for Creative Intelligence. Will Jensen and Lori Huang still put their names together on arts organizations after all that’s happened? And if there is no Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang College of Art, Architecture and Design, what will happen to Vanderbilt’s SF campus when it opens next year?

The CCA was started in 1907, and Huang and his wife were expected to support its transition to a new chapter. It would be a shame if this is how it ends. Reps at Vanderbilt didn’t get back to me.

It’s a new era in Tribeca. Tonight, Karma, a burgeoning mega-gallery with spaces in New York’s Chelsea and LA’s Hollywood, opens its new gallery at 38 White Street. Founder Brendan Dugan and director Siniša Mačković took me on a tour earlier this week, and it’s easily one of the most generous spaces anywhere in the neighborhood. Plus, an outpost of Karma Bookstore—a much needed bookstore for a neighborhood shockingly lacking in one—is coming in right across the street.

This will be the latest big-tent blue chipper to take a space in the Triangle Below Canal, as they used to call this neighborhood. Something to consider: In the last few years, mega-galleries such as David Zwirner and Hauser & Wirth have shut their uptown townhouses and opened downtown.

Also opening tonight is a White Street outpost of Gratin gallery, which has a roster of incredibly exciting young stars, including Lorenzo Amos (whom we wrote about a year ago). I’m hearing about other younger dealers grabbing spaces in the neighborhood. The art market isn’t exactly on fire, but dealers are betting on one thing: the enduring power and capital of New York City.

Speaking of New York, guess who’s lived here full-time for almost a year? Steven Spielberg, that’s who. On New Year’s Day 2026, the GOAT American director—who is married to the artist Kate Capshaw—moved his official residence from California to New York, and has made the apartment in the San Remo his home base. You will not be surprised to hear that, post-move, Spielberg is doing extremely cool stuff in town. He’s walking around with a script and a Tracy Kidder book while slugging down an iced McCafé. He’s getting lunch at Benvenuto Cafe. He’s having Mayor Zohran Mamdani over to the crib.

The only thing left was for one of the city’s great museums to throw a big party for the Hollywood-royalty-gone-Gotham. Last night, Spielberg got just that: He was honored at the MoMA Film Benefit, sponsored by Chanel. I was there. Read the full report—with fun pictures!—here.

Also on VF this week: an exclusive excerpt from an uproarious new memoir by artist Jessica Craig-Martin, I Regret I am Able to Attend. Craig-Martin is a real treasure of the art world, a great photographer—and, as it turns out, a hell of a writer. The whole book is a compulsively readable blast. The chapter where Craig-Martin recalls working as an extremely inexperienced, occasionally larcenous teller at Dean & DeLuca is one of the funniest, most satisfying New York vignettes I’ve read this year. And of course, all the scuttlebutt from the ’80s art scene is fabulous. Read the excerpt, in which our narrator spills all the tea—and, um, stuff stronger than tea—about working as a waitress when Indochine opened.

Happy 80th birthday to the great painter Stanley Whitney. His wife, the artist Marina Adams, and son, dealer Will Whitney, threw Stanley a party to celebrate his octogenarian status on Nine Orchard’s roof, overlooking Dimes Square. Writers, artists, dealers, old heads, everyone was there. A fabulous Wednesday night.

#3614. GTA 6 And These Other Games Can Justify An $80 Price, Expert Says

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 finally releases on November 19, and you'll have to pay at least $80 for it. That's a full $20 more than what GTA 5 cost in 2013 and $10 more than many other big AAA games today. Is $80 going to become the "new normal" for AAA games, or is it, along with Nintendo's Mario Kart World and Tears of the Kingdom for Switch 2, an outlier at $80?

According to Alinea Analytics researcher Rhys Elliott, $80 won't be an across-the-board new price for all games. Some developers will purposefully price their games lower to draw in more consumers--he pointed to games like Expedition 33 ($50), Phantom Blade Zero ($60), and Oblivion Remastered ($50) as examples.

Elliott said that when GTA 6 inevitably becomes a huge success with its $80 and $100 editions, some publishers will be "jumping for joy" because they'll take this as a signal that the market will indeed accept these higher prices.

However, Elliott said he hopes the industry doesn't learn the wrong lessons from GTA 6 and its $80 price point. "GTA 6 is as inelastic as things get in entertainment. People will pay anything to get their mitts on this one, which makes it seem like the perfect Trojan horse for an industry-wide price rise," he said.

"The $80 price point will be a Godsend to some publishers, but it’ll be a snowball's chance in hell for others. After all, this kind of stuff can be zero-sum. When a player spends $100 on GTA 6, their remaining budget shrinks," he added.

Elliott went on to list off some of the studios and game franchises that could likely get their fanbases to buy in at $80. He said these include the next big God of War game after Laufey, the next Naughty Dog game, Intergalactic: The Heretic Prophet, and future Forza titles (assuming Xbox strips them out of Game Pass). Additionally, Elliott said From Software "has the cache" to charge $80 for its new games, while Hogwarts Legacy 2 could also up the price to $80. Elliott added that some of the top sports games could charge more, but that might be a tougher sell considering those games are full of microtransactions already.

"So not all games were created equal, and mid-tier AAA publishers--and also bigger publishers offering smaller games or remakes--will price downward at $40-$60," Elliott said.

There are a lot of factors at play here. For starters, GTA 5 launched at $60 back in 2013, and that same $60 is worth $86 today after inflation, making GTA 6--at least its $80 edition--effectively cheaper than GTA 5.

At the same time, many people are acutely aware that their pay has not kept up with inflation, while the federal minimum wage hasn't moved up since 2009. GTA 6 is also coming out at a rough time for many people, with gas and grocery prices surging, and the cost of everyday goods generally spiking due in part to increasing inflation. And anyone heading to a store to buy a console to play GTA 6 on is in for some serious sticker shock, as game consoles today are more expensive than ever due to the AI craze.

New video games generally staying the same price over the years has had serious negative effects on the entire industry, experts have said. It's part of the reason why publishers now try to squeeze people more with DLC, battle passes, microtransactions, collector's editions, paid early access, and more. Recently, an Xbox advertising chief said price increases would be a hard sell, so the company is turning to ads to help offset ballooning budgets and keep the business healthy.

One of the best headphone deals right now is for my favorite headphones: Sony's 1000X series has been around since 2016, with each new model improving on the previous iteration, the latest being the Sony WH-1000XM6, released in 2025. #3611. Official Zelda Website Raises Eyebrows By Labeling 3DS Game As Playable On Switch

Nintendo is celebrating The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary in many different ways, but one detail on the company's official website raised confusion--and curiosity-- about a classic 3DS Zelda game.

A "History" page on Nintendo's website lists every mainline Zelda game in release order, including the release date and which platforms you can play for each entry. The site marks every game that's playable for Nintendo Switch Online subscribers--and the 2013 3DS game The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds was marked as such. The NSO icon has since been removed from the site.

Currently, the Nintendo Classics library allows NSO subscribers to play select NES, SNES, and Game Boy games, while the Expansion Pack subscription includes access to Nintendo 64, Game Boy Advance, GameCube, and Virtual Boy games. There's currently no way to play 3DS games on Nintendo Switch, prompting the question of whether this was an error on Nintendo's website or an accidental leak that A Link Between Worlds will somehow be playable on Switch. GameSpot has reached out to Nintendo for clarification on the matter.

The site appropriately labels the Zelda games featured on Nintendo Classics if they are only playable with the Nintendo Switch Online Expansion Pack subscription, which applies to Ocarina of Time (the original), Majora's Mask, A Link to the Past/Four Swords on GBA, The Wind Waker, and The Minish Cap.

If this labeling for A Link Between Worlds were true, it would be surprising if the Expansion Pack were not required to play it. Nintendo Classics also lacks any Wii or DS games, so jumping straight to 3DS would be a bizarre move for the service.

Whatever the case, A Link Between Worlds is a magnificent entry in the Zelda series that deserves to be experienced. GameSpot's 9/10 review of the game called it an "absolute treat to play" with some of the "best Zelda dungeons in years."

The Governors Awards kick off awards season these days, which means some of Hollywood’s best and brightest trekked across Los Angeles in a bunch of finery to walk the red carpet – or in this case, blue carpet. Some big names from Zendaya to Florence Pugh to Timothèe Chalamet and Glenn Close debuted some memorable celebrity fashion, and I just want to talk about some of the bold looks.

Florence Pugh has been on a very romantic kick lately promoting East of Eden. She’s worn Victorian blouses with big ruffles, and there’s been a lot of puff in her sleeves lately. She did the opposite for the 17th annual Governors Awards. Her satin dress was form-fitting and very different than what we’ve seen her in promoting her Netflix show. But we’re getting close to Dunesday season, baby.

The dress was yet another winner from Valentino, who also made Pugh's infamous sheer dress. I'm still thinking about its ethereal nature.

Charlize Theron also opted for a memorable color. She paired a red curve-hugging dress from Tom Ford with a red lip, and I just can’t stop looking at it. Plus there’s nothing like posing with your dog next to a bathtub to give a little extra allure.

A post shared by Charlize Theron (@charlizeafrica)

Both looks were well-recieved, and lots of fans commented to Charlize with something along the lines of, “Red is definitely your color!” I mean, I can’t disagree with that.

Some did call Zendaya’s brown dress with hip pads “flawless,” while other comments mentioned it’s “giving sophistication and allure." Another post mentioned she could “wear a trashcan” and she’d still look “glamorous.” (Though that’s more of a compliment to Zendaya than the dress.) A subset of people also said Zendaya understood the assignment, as she’s doubtless wearing earth tones to kick off the Dune: Part 3 press tour, but some fans just could not get over the way the dress moved and hung, and the color also seemed to be an issue for some.

Some of the comments about the dress itself noted it was a rare miss in her longstanding collaboration with Law Roach.

Zendaya takes so many fashion risks. She’s done the whole tennis method dressing thing. She once wore a C-3PO armored look and that was seemingly less divisive than this brown dress. I like that she tried something weird with these little side panniers. Despite it being vintage, I’ve certainly not seen much like it on the red carpet, and if this is her kicking off the Dune press tour, it’s certainly a memorable way to begin.

But did it smolder as much as Pugh and Theron? OK probably not.

#3609. Kirk Cousins Gets Emotional After Blowout Win in Triumphant Vikings Return

Kirk Cousins was noticeably overcome by the moment following a dominant win over the Green Bay Packers in his return to the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, November 15.

“It was emotional coming to the stadium,” Cousins, 38, told ESPN’s Lindsey Thiry on the field at Green Bay’s Lambeau Field after the Vikings’ 30-10 victory. “Three years ago, tearing my Achilles here. It’s been a tough three years. I was just grateful for the opportunity to play here today, and grateful for my teammates and what they did to make this outcome possible.”

Cousins was traded back to the Vikings from the Las Vegas Raiders on Wednesday, November 11.

The quarterback previously played for Minnesota for six seasons from 2018 to 2023. His final game as a member of the Vikings came in October 2023, when he tore his right Achilles tendon in a game against the Packers. Cousins spent the next two seasons with the Atlanta Falcons before signing with the Raiders in April.

While acknowledging the symbolism of the moment, Cousins urged, “There’s so much football up ahead.”

“Certainly it’s gratifying to be able to come back here with the purple on,” Cousins added. “I think to come back here with another team isn’t quite the same. To come back here with the purple on, similar time of year, three years later, it’s a blessing, to be able to have a win like we had today.”

The Vikings (7-2) are currently tied for first place in the NFC North with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears. With the loss on Sunday, the Packers sit alone in fourth place at 6-4.

An emotional Kirk Cousins, in his return to the Vikings at Lambeau Field: “I tore my Achilles here and it’s been a tough three years…” pic.twitter.com/8PhbEVs7Oq

— Lindsey Thiry (@LindseyThiry) November 15, 2026

Cousins and the Vikings return to action when they host the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, November 22.

“He’s always been mature,” Minnesota head coach, Kevin O’Connell, said of Cousins’ performance. “He’s always been meticulous in his preparation. He’s always done everything in his power to prepare himself for games. But there was a level of poise. It never felt like at any point from the time we talked on the phone [before the trade] all the way through to giving him a game ball today, where it was anything other than just rock solid, consistent.”

Cousins finished 21-for-31 passing for 207 yards with two touchdowns and one interception.

Vikings wide receiver Justin Jefferson said Cousins “did what we needed him to do.”

“It wasn’t really too much of big shots down the field, but it was just dumping it off and getting those extra three, four yards after the catch,” Jefferson, 27, told reporters after the game. “So it was definitely great for us. And his composure, his confidence in the huddle, all of that, it definitely created a positive vibe in the huddle.”

#3608. You Can Probably Guess WoW: Forever’s Most Popular Race, Class, And Faction

World of Warcraft: Forever has been in the wild for one week, and now we have all kinds of stats to sink our teeth into as they relate to the most popular races, classes, and faction in the latest version of developer Blizzard's MMORPG.

Forever launched November 4, becoming the biggest launch in WoW history by concurrent and returning players. Aside from that fact, Blizzard hasn't shared additional information on exactly how many characters have been made or what classes are most popular.

For that, we turn to Raider.IO, a WoW stat-tracking website more commonly used in the modern version of the game to provide rankings and details related to raids and Mythic+ progression. 

According to the site, close to 3.9 million characters have been created across all regions and rulesets so far. Around 48% of those characters are on the Alliance, with nearly 52% being on the Horde.

The most popular two races aren't all that surprising--undead and humans. Despite being the most boring choice imaginable, humans have always been a popular choice in WoW Classic thanks to their strong passives and the ability to be most classes. In Forever, they currently make up 37% of the Alliance population. Undead, on the other hand, are getting a massive boost from being the only Horde race to currently have access to Paladin. They make up nearly 40% of the Horde.

It won't shock you to learn then that Paladin is Forever's most-played class, with undead Paladin being the most-played race-and-class combo.

Skyborne elves are WoW's newest playable race, available to both factions. Around 10% of all characters are Skyborne, and faction-wise they are fairly even. Around 10% of Skyborne are Alliance and close to 11% are on the Horde. Consdiering how popular blood elves are in other versions of the game, the number of Skyborne feels low by comparison, though the fact they cost $30 to access probably has something to do with that.

As for what rulesets are most popular, the normal (PvE) server is far and away the biggest, with over 2 million characters. The PvP ruleset isn't too far behind with around 1.5 million characters. Those two rulesets dwarf the size of the game's two RP rulesets, which combined have around 250,000 players. 

With the exception of standard RP, every ruleset has a larger Horde population, a subject Blizzard recently commented on officially. In a forum post, Blizzard announced its goal is for PvP servers to be as close to 50/50 faction balance as possible, and would be placing restrictions on creating Horde characters on PvP rulesets in an effort to make that a reality.

"World of Warcraft: Forever's PvP is at its best when the Alliance and Horde are on equal footing, and we are dedicated to helping maintain that balance so that we can all witness battles at the epic scale that has made WoW: Forever PvP so memorable thus far," Blizzard said.  

One week after WoW: Forever's shockingly smooth launch, we've been impressed how visual updates and Blizzard's changes to the classic WoW formula have made the MMO feel brand new again. Forever received its first major class and dungeon changes earlier this week.

#3607. Martin McDonagh Calls Sam Rockwell “One of the Best Actors of His Generation, If Not the Best”

Director Martin McDonagh has become as well-known for making memorable films as he is for writing the complex male friendships within them.

"I like mining down into the sensitivity that I think a lot of male relationships do have, but aren't as – especially in American films – explored sensitively," he said about the subject during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. "It's not just a buddy film, and it's not a romance, and it's not just about cool CIA guys," McDonagh continued. “It's sort of the opposite in other ways. And that I think is interesting to explore because I think my male relationships are that way. They can be sensitive and sad and happy and all the things that a female relationship can be. So I think that's why I keep coming back to it.”

The conversation, which featured McDonagh and the film’s stars John Malkovich and Mariana di Girolamo, was moderated by VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford following an exclusive screening of their new film, Wild Horse Nine. The acclaimed dark comedy follows two CIA agents (Malkovich and Sam Rockwell) who are not only behind the plan to overthrow the Chilean government in 1973, but have also had a hand in several other significant historical moments in the US and abroad.

Maria di Girolamo, John Malkovich and Martin McDonagh, in conversation with Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on Friday, November 13, 2026.

Malkovich and Rockwell's characters engage in pithy, often hilarious banter throughout the film, and their onscreen chemistry is a highlight.

John Malkovich at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

"I love Sam," said Malkovich. “I knew him a bit socially before this, but I'd worked with him once before, which was a great pleasure on a film called A Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy. He's like a kind of expert trainer at SeaWorld who can get the whales and the sharks and the dolphins to show things in exchange for a fish. And Sam is a great student of acting. He is a great student of film and of theater, and he's great fun, very hardworking, and just an ideal colleague. I couldn't imagine a better colleague than Sam and I've had some excellent colleagues.”

"He's one of the best actors of his generation, if not the best," adds McDonagh of Rockwell. "He's always surprising, always dangerous, always sensitive, always smart, always coming up with new stuff. And I think there's a danger to him that's lovely to write for. We always hope the characters will always be surprising, and with Sam's voice in the head, that really helps."

Mariana di Girolamo at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For rising star Mariana di Girolamo, a Chilean actress making her English language movie debut with Wild Horse Nine, she was excited and only slightly intimidated to be a part of the cast.

"It was quite a challenge to perform for the first time in English," she said. "I prepared myself with a coach and we rehearsed with John, Sam and Parker [Posey] and Ailin [Salas] in a public theater in New York where I heard the script for the first time. That was amazing for me, for us." di Girolamo, who is very familiar with the fraught period of Chilean history depicted in the film, said she appreciated how McDonagh put it all in context. "It was my first time approaching that period of time in this way with this very beautiful dark humor. I was laughing about these things and feeling empathy with these CIA agents that committed a lot of horrific, horrific things. I've never read something like that, and the arc of my character is so beautiful, unique, I really wanted to be part of this."

Martin McDonagh at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

A price drop always stands out more when the product in question already has a reputation for delivering above its size, and that’s the case with the Bose SoundLink Plus. It hasn’t been on the market for long, but it’s already earned strong reviews—CNET labeled it “the Goldilocks of Bose Bluetooth speakers.” And right now, ahead of Black Friday, it’s down to $179 from $269, which price trackers show is the lowest it’s ever been.

Bose positions it right in the middle of the SoundLink lineup, and you feel that balance in how it’s built. It’s compact enough to clip onto a backpack using its built-in nylon strap, and tough enough to handle getting knocked around, and sealed against dust and full water submersion with an IP67 rating. Battery life can last up to 20 hours, depending on the volume, which is sufficient for full-day outings. On the connectivity side, there’s Bluetooth 5.4 with AAC and AptX Adaptive support, as well as the ability to keep two devices paired for smoother switching. What you don’t get is a microphone, an aux port, or any voice assistant support, which is worth considering if you prefer wired options or use speakers for calls.

As for its sound profile, it leans into mid- and high-bass, which gives electronic and pop tracks a lively pulse, though at higher volumes, you may notice some compression (which is common in speakers this size). It also doesn’t reach into true low-bass territory, so anyone who wants thumping sub-bass may not get it here, but the punch it does deliver feels clean for its size, notes this PCMag review. And while you won't get the width and separation of a stereo mix since the SoundLink Plus plays audio in mono, its directivity is good—meaning its sound remains clear from different listening positions, so you don't have to sit directly in front of it to get a good experience.

#3605. GTA 6 Could Sell 55 Million Copies By Early Next Year, Report Says, And Average Selling Price Could Be $90

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to be a gigantic commercial success, but just how big will the launch be? Investor's Business Daily compiled data from a series of analyst reports about the game and its owner, Take-Two, and the consensus is that it's going to be a juggernaut.

In terms of sales, Brian Pitz of BMO Capital Markets said GTA 6 could sell 55 million copies during Take-Two's fiscal 2027, which ends on March 31, 2027. He said the game could sell 45 million units alone during the game's launch quarter, which is well ahead of the estimates of 34.2 million that IBD compiled.

 "This is an outlier in every respect," Circana's Mat Piscatella told the publication. "There have been some big game launches in the past, but nothing quite at this scale, not only in terms of the investment, but in terms of the anticipation. It's in its own league."

GTA 6 is launching with an $80 standard edition and a $100 Ultimate Edition. Raymond James analyst Andrew Marok said he's forecasting 50 million unit sales for the fiscal year 2027, and that the blended average selling price will be close to $90. According to Sensor Tower, early data suggested preorders were skewing toward the $100 edition, but by launch, it could be around 50/50.

Matthew Cost of Morgan Stanley, meanwhile, said if GTA 6 does indeed have strong sales out of the gate, this could create a "large potential audience" for the next iteration of GTA Online. Rockstar has not said anything yet about an online mode for GTA 6, but given the huge success of GTA Online for GTA 5, it's all but guaranteed that GTA 6 will incorporate online multiplayer as well.

Cost said this is a big deal for investors and may represent "the next major catalyst" for Take-Two's stock price. Take-Two's share price is down about 10% so far in 2026, and currently trades around $228/share..

A new version of GTA Online for GTA 6 would no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways to spend more money, and that could be frustrating for fans but great news for investors who want to see bigger returns.

D.A. Davidson analyst Wyatt Swanson said Take-Two's share price could surge to $300 in part because he believes Rockstar will release a PC edition of GTA 6 and usher in GTA Online 2.0. These releases would "enable structurally higher margins" for Take-Two, he said.

According to Sensor Tower, GTA 6 has already sold 12 million copies and generated $1.2 billion in revenue. GTA 5, meanwhile, took 72 hours to clear $1 billion in revenue--GTA 6 reached that a week before release, apparently.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.

Bowen Yang made a surprise cameo on Saturday Night Live this past weekend. The beloved former cast member appeared in multiple sketches, first as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during the cold open and later as Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel in John Mulaney’s wild musical number about New York City. Yang seemed comfortable and back in his element, but it turns out the behind the scenes wasn’t exactly smooth sailing. Sarah Sherman actually had to fill in for him during dress rehearsal, leading to a hilarious visual that’s making the rounds.

Yang is currently crushing it as Mary Todd Lincoln in the Broadway production of Oh, Mary! His schedule on the show, however, isn’t exactly SNL friendly. The Lyceum Theatre offers two performances every Saturday: one at 5 PM and one at 8:30 PM. Since SNL’s dress rehearsal starts at 8 PM, there was no way for the actor to appear in both; so, during the cold open, Sarah Sherman appeared in Yang’s part, hilariously wearing a sign that said Bowen Yang. According to Late Nighter, Marcello Hernández warned the crowd ahead of time, though I can’t imagine they expected this visual, which Yang later posted to his Instagram account…

A post shared by Bowen Yang (@fayedunaway)

It’s unclear exactly when the details of Yang’s appearance came together, but he reportedly did head to Studio 8H after his Broadway show on Friday to do a rehearsal for his two scenes. I can’t imagine longtime showrunner Lorne Michaels would be okay with a random celebrity doing a cameo without the standard rehearsing schedule, but he obviously knows Bowen well enough to know he didn’t need the full runthrough.

He clearly didn’t either, as he was a standout during the live show in both the cold open and as Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel in the musical number. Saidah Belo-Osagie reportedly played the second part very capably during the dress rehearsal, but that was never going to work for the live show. She had another role in the sketch, and also, Mary Todd Lincoln Tunnel was clearly written for Yang, as he’s currently playing Mary Todd Lincoln in the aforementioned show. He probably would have been personally offended if he wasn’t asked and tuned into SNL to see someone else doing an outrageous take on the part he’s currently playing on Broadway.

We’ve gotten two consecutive weeks with cameos from former cast members, as Bobby Moynihan appeared in the Davis S Pumpkins anniversary sketch and in a segment on Weekend Update as Drunk Uncle. Personally, I’d love to see SNL try and do double appearances more often. It’s always fun to see old favorites surprise fans by appearing in a sketch, but it’s even more fun to see those familiar faces show up twice during the same episode so they have a little more to do.

SNL is currently on hiatus for a few weeks, but it’ll return in early December with a new episode hosted by Amanda Seyfried. I cannot wait, as she should bring something new and exciting to 30 Rock and will hopefully continue the momentum as the show has recently dropped its strongest episodes of the season, including this past weekend's heater where John Mulaney brought some of the sharpest social commentary we've gotten in a long time.

#3603. GTA 6 Owner Take-Two Is Not Interested In Selling Itself After EA Goes Private For $55 Billion

Recently, the gaming giant Electronic Arts was taken private in a $55 billion sale to an investor consortium led by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund. Could GTA 6 owner Take-Two be the next big company that gets acquired? Don't bet on it, CEO Strauss Zelnick says.

Speaking to David Rubenstein, Zelnick said Take-Two's business results have proven that it "can do very well as an independent company."

He said Take-Two's business is already "at scale" and healthy enough financially with a "terrific balance sheet," as he put it.

"We are not in a place where we need to be part of a bigger organization to be competitive. And in the entertainment business, scale matters," he said.

Zelnick said companies that do less than a billion in annual revenue might have issues with developing, marketing, and distributing games at scale. Not only that, but companies that don't generate a lot of money might not be able to survive the realities of the creative business, in which sometimes your product flops.

"But once you're over a billion dollars in annual revenue, and we're way beyond that point. Our guidance is $8 billion to $8.2 billion this fiscal year, additional scale doesn't seem to help you succeed."

In early 2008, Electronic Arts privately pursued a buyout of Take-Two, but after the GTA and BioShock company rejected it, EA went public in an attempt to get a deal done. Later that year, EA abandoned its plans to try to buy Take-Two after the GTA company said it was worth more and EA refused to increase its bid.

In 2019, it was rumored that Sony was attempting to buy Take-Two, but that was ultimately deemed to be unconfirmed market chatter and not a formal bid.

Take-Two has a market cap of more than $42 billion, and that is expected to grow in the year ahead, so it would seemingly take a lot of money to convince Take-Two to sell. Going forward, Zelnick has teased that new GTA games could release even faster, and that could be a positive for the company's financials.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. Preloading is underway now, and that's good news because the game has a massive file size.

#3602. Husband Kills Wife Before Dying by Suicide in Sheriff's Office Parking Lot

Authorities in Mississippi confirmed that a husband was going to turn himself in for killing his wife before he died by suicide on Saturday, November 14.

The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office confirmed in a press release obtained by Us that the victims were identified as married couple Alanitra Adam-Banks and James Banks, who both lived in Robinsonville, Mississippi.

Authorities learned of the incident when deputies received a call on Saturday around 12:51 p.m. regarding someone who had been shot at the Lexington apartments in Robinsonville. The caller – who has not been identified – reportedly told officers that Banks, 54, had allegedly shot Adam-Banks, 31.

Upon their arrival, deputies found Adam-Banks suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. Pafford emergency medical personnel tried to revive and treat Adam-Banks’ injuries before the Tunica County coroner ultimately declared her dead at the scene.

After Banks was identified as the shooter, authorities managed to get in contact with him on a phone call and he reportedly told authorities that he was on his way to the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office.

Deputies later found Banks’ vehicle in the Sheriff’s Office parking lot and discovered that he had died by suicide, according to the press release.

Authorities said that the deputies and first responders attempted lifesaving measures on Banks, though he was eventually declared dead at the scene.

The Sheriff’s Office went on to say that the investigation into the killings remains ongoing and that the case was being investigated as a homicide-suicide.

Despite confirming the deaths, authorities have not yet released information regarding the events that led up to the shooting. It’s also not currently known if Banks and Adam-Banks had a history of domestic violence disputes in the past or if officers believe Banks had a motive in killing his wife.

Details about their marriage have also not been shared, including how long the couple was together, when they got married and if they shared any children.

The Tunica County Sheriff’s Office had no additional information to share about the findings of the investigation when contacted by Us about updates in the case.

Police are seeking information from the public and have asked that anyone with knowledge regarding the incident contact the Tunica County Sheriff’s Office at 662-363-1411.

#3601. Eight 'Winter Arc' Rules That Will Actually Deliver Results

There are a lot of terrible social media trends out there aimed at self-improvement, yet even though everybody has been making fun of the "Winter Arc" craze, I actually think it’s a good one. During your Winter Arc, you promise yourself you’ll stick to your fitness and self-care routines during (and despite) the end-of-year chaos. It's a good goal, with one caveat: Make sure you choose rules that will actually improve your life and deliver results.

Think of the “arc” in the sense of a “story arc.” The Winter Arc is a self-improvement journey that unfolds over the last few months of the calendar year. The most hardcore #gymtok-ers will tell you the Winter Arc officially begins on Oct. 1, but others start in early November, or whenever they get around to it. The "when" isn't critical, though—whenever you read this is a fine time to start. The close of the Winter Arc is fixed, however: It ends Jan. 1, just as everybody who is less dedicated than you is waking from their holiday food comas and resolving to get in shape.

You get to choose your own terms for your Winter Arc. The general vibe is one of locking in, committing to your goals, and actually doing the things you’re always saying you’ll do. TikToker @carlyupgraded has said that her own mental image of someone nailing their Winter Arc is “hood up, headphones on, getting ready to go for a run in the rain at 5 a.m.”

It turns out I’ve accidentally been Winter-Arc-ing for years; I just didn’t know it had a catchy name. Why save your gym routine for New Year’s when you’ll have the place to yourself all December? We’re even gifted with an extra hour in the mornings to fill with something productive.

I really love the mindset shift involved. Commonly, people are active in the summer (great time for outdoor fun), may or may not stick with their routines in the fall, and let everything fall apart as the holidays approach. Who has time to go to the gym when you’re planning Thanksgiving, attending holiday parties, studying for final exams, or whatever else the end of the year throws in front of you?

But that’s the exact reason why this time of year is the best to start (or restart) a fitness routine, or really any kind of routine. When you start a routine during a busy time of year, you’ll be forced to make it sustainable. The gym routine you can stick with amid the chaos isn’t going to be one you drop after a few months. You’re already training yourself to work around obstacles as they come up, which is a key component of self-efficacy. And when the chaos clears on Jan. 1, your routine will be even easier to stick to.

Of course, there are ways to lean in too hard: Choosing unsustainable habits, falling for bad diet advice, mistaking not masturbating for some kind of health hack, the usual suspects. There’s also the pitfall of focusing too much on the vibes and too little on what you’re actually going to do or how you’ll benefit.

And then there’s the framing: You were working on yourself all year, but you’re in danger of letting up on the gas, but you’re committed to locking in so that you’re a step ahead of everybody who takes this time to slack off. I really don’t love this tack. Self-improvement is not a competition. There’s a difference between being consistent in your training and healthy eating (good) and seeing the pursuit of health and fitness as something where you always have to work harder because you’re at risk of getting left behind.

I also don’t love how gendered the Winter Arc TikToks tend to be. When you search for Winter Arc content, the first few suggestions include “winter arc for women” and “winter arc for men.” When I first started looking at the Winter Arc trend a few years ago, the women’s versions were more likely to include restrictive dieting or to focus on how the Winter Arc will finally (sigh) snatch your waist. These days, the focus is more on personal goal setting: Lots of the girlies filming their Winter Arc rules are doing so in a notebook and talking about journaling exercises that will help you identify what you need to work on to get to your "best self." Sometimes this is all monetized; training plans and journaling prompts can, of course, be purchased at the link in bio.

I do like that many of the women’s versions emphasize sustainability and setting your own goals rather than copying somebody else's. I don't love the enormity of the mental burden you're supposed to shoulder before even beginning. Should I really have to file an in-depth written report with myself before revamping every area of my life with a 100% commitment to multiple goals?

The men’s versions tend to go off the rails in another direction, with rules like “no girls” or “go ghost.” No distractions! Here, I've seen a shift over the years as well: at first there was overly serious content, followed quickly by satire (yelling at the viewer to get divorced and go work out in the dark). Now the men's videos tend to be more vibes-based, featuring images of pre-dawn workouts and plates full of salad with motivational quotes playing in the background. When the men give their rules, they tend to be simpler than the women's—no journaling exercises—but they often boil down to the same overly strict routines. (And then, of course, they'll offer to sell you a 90-day or 60-day plan.)

If you’re going to do a Winter Arc (or if you’re already doing one), make sure to structure it in a way that benefits you. Choosing 10 overly ambitious goals and setting yourself up for failure is not a healthy way to approach self-improvement, OK? Pick goals that are meaningful, achievable without divine intervention, and trackable with tools you already have at hand (for example, tracking your steps with a Fitbit or your running mileage with a Garmin watch).

It’s also helpful to think of developing yourself over this arc, rather than taking it as a three-month (or two-month) challenge where you have to do everything right all the time. If you currently wake up at 8 a.m. and want to wake up at 5 a.m., you don’t have to set your alarm for 5 a.m. tomorrow. It’s OK to aim for 7:30 a.m., make that a habit, then try for 7:00 a.m., and so on.

With that in mind, here are some "rules" I've seen from creators that I'm actually on board with (so long as you don't overwhelm yourself with them):

Wake up earlier. A great goal, especially if you take advantage of the time change to make things easier on your body.

Get to bed on time. Never a bad idea. Cultivating good sleep habits in general is always worthwhile.

Get your steps in. Be thoughtful about what your target is: 10,000 is not for everybody. Better to choose a number that would be a modest improvement on what you already do.

Exercise X times per week. Pick a number that works for you, and get into it. Be realistic about your goal, and for the best results, be consistent even if you’re sore at first.

Eat healthy. This is a great goal, with the major caveat that there are a lot of ways to eat healthy. You don’t need to cut out sugar or pretend that there’s something evil about seed oils. Do get more protein and veggies.

Be more thoughtful about using social media. I’m not going to tell you to delete all your apps (“except TikTok,” as the TikTokers say). But it’s fair to consider whether you might want to delete a few apps, turn off some notifications, or put your phone on Do Not Disturb for more hours of the day.

Journal or read more. Journaling can be great for working through your feelings or cultivating a creative habit. Reading can be entertainment or a great way to learn. Choose whichever you need most.

Learn a new skill. I’ve mostly seen this one in the men’s TikToks, and I love it. They’re often thinking of “skills” that will help in some kind of entrepreneurship grift they’re about to sell you, but there are tons of skills that will come in handy in life, or that are at least fun to learn. Practice a language, get better at cooking, make some art. Skills are, as I’ve noted, a multi-layered exercise for your brain. And they may come in handy someday.

This year I've slacked off on my fitness routine as I've gotten more involved in other hobbies, but I'm actually looking forward to being more consistent. My winter goals include exercising early in the day when possible and reading 20 minutes each day. (I'm even tracking the second one with a sticker chart.)

#3600. Andrew Scott On What Makes Elsinore “So Moving”

Although the emotional core of Elsinore is centered around beloved actor Ian Charleston dealing with terminal illness, its star Andrew Scott says the film has as much heart as it does humor.

“The most singular thing about our film I think is the humor in it,” he said during a panel conversation at the inaugural Vanity Fair Screening Room at LACMA on Friday. “The tragedy in some ways is a little bit like Hamlet itself, but you can't make a film about Ian Charleston without having gags in it. He was incredibly funny. Every person [who knew him] said he was just wickedly funny, and flirtatious, and he was always looking towards the light, and he had a certain degree of courage. So that is something I think that we all share as a sense of humor.”

Andrew Scott, Billie Piper, Stephen Beresford and Rebecca Ford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

Elsinore tells the story of Scottish actor Ian Charleson (Scott) who attempts to perform Hamlet at the National Theatre while secretly living with AIDS. Scott has received early acclaim for his powerful portrayal of Charleson. Before the film began Vanity Fair’s West Coast Editor John Ross warned the audience that "first you're going to laugh, then you're going to cry," while watching Scott’s performance.

“I think … why the film is so moving is because [Charleson’s] not wallowing at any point. He was insanely courageous,” continued Scott. “So that to me was the thing that we were the most

insistent on in some ways. And that's really all down to finding actors who in this extraordinary ensemble have a really terrific sense of humor. And we kind of knew that we could, with the screenplay, get the best actors in the country. And I feel we did.”

The panel conversation featured Scott, costar Billie Piper, and writer Stephen Beresford, moderated by VF's Senior Hollywood Correspondent Rebecca Ford, following an exclusive screening of the film.

Billie Piper at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026

For Piper, who plays Charleston's close friend Patsy, she relied heavily on Beresford's script for her prep, as well as information she gleaned from those who actually knew Patsy, and Charleston.

“I've spoken to a few members of the family, their friends, and then I sort of cherry-picked things from people I'd known in the beginning of my career, the louder figures in our industry,” she said. “And then I did my own interpretation and just had a good time. It's a very moving story, but I had a lot of fun playing that part. She's a really joyful character to play, I enjoyed the comedy. And I understand that a lot of her jokes are coming from a place of despair.”

Beresford, who has known Scott for 25 years, said he didn't initially think of his longtime friend for the role, but should have.

“The story of Ian, and Ian's Hamlet [performance] is legendary in the British theater,” he said. “So many people said it was the greatest Hamlet they'd ever seen, and that it had this incredible quality. So I knew about the story, and then it was brought to me actually as an idea by a producer who said, ‘What about writing about Ian Charleston, and what about Andrew playing Ian Charleston?’ And then I just thought, ‘Well, why didn't I have that idea myself five years ago?’ So yeah, that's really how it happened, and I started to research it, the details of the story were so incredible, and so moving.”

Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

Scott, who famously played Hamlet onstage 150 times beginning in 2017, prior to filming Elsinore, closed out the panel conversation by reciting his favorite line from the classic tragedy.

“When Hamlet says the line about the war that was going on—and this was written 400 years ago—it just seems so relevant to what he might have been experiencing at the time, which is: ‘I see the imminent death of 20,000 men who for a fantasy, a trick of fame, go to their graves like beds.’ The idea that that was written 400 years ago, and that he was watching 50 percent of his friends die for no reason and be neglected by governments, and derided by the public. And it was just happening, and happening time and time again.”

Scott continued: “The reason that I love it so much is that when I was doing Hamlet myself, of course I wasn't thinking about the AIDS crisis, but the enduring nature of art, something that was written 400 years ago by Shakespeare, could actually be of use to somebody in 1989 and then be reproduced again in 2026 and be of use. And that idea of art being useful down the lines is so moving to me.”

Vanity Fair's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, Elsinore stars Andrew Scott and Billie Piper and writer Stephen Beresford at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 13, 2026.

#3599. “Physical” GTA 6 Copies Might Be Vulnerable To A Very Stupid But Serious Trick

Grand Theft Auto 6 ditched traditional discs for its "physical" launch, with Rockstar's game being sold as a digital code-in-box at retailers beginning this week. However, it appears a packaging choice may have accidentally left the game vulnerable to thieves--assuming they have a flashlight.

As shared on the forum ResetEra, users who received a physical version of Grand Theft Auto 6, at least in PEGI regions, report that the game's download code is printed directly on the inside of the cover rather than on a card or separate insert. When a flashlight is focused on the cover from the outside of the closed game case, the download code is visible in reverse.

In other words, there's a serious risk people could go into a store, do this trick, redeem the code, and leave the poor soul who actually buys the game off the shelf without GTA 6.

At this time, the trick does not seem to work on North American copies of GTA 6, as the code is intentionally obscured. Why Rockstar would not use this strategy on all regions is unclear. We've reached out to Rockstar for an explanation and will update this post if and when we receive a response.

If you happen to get your GTA 6 code stolen after paying $80, you can at least sleep soundly knowing that the thief can't play the game yet. Code-in-box copies, as well as digital preorders, all unlock for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S on November 19.

Sing Sing was one of my favorite movies of 2024 and one of the best movies of that year. Colman Domingo shines. He once again proves that he’s one of the best actors of his generation. Domingo’s brilliant scene partners, many not professionally trained actors, magnify his performance.

Using former Sing Sing Prison inmates, and some of those the story was based on, was a revolutionary idea. When I saw Union County, I became more convinced that films should enlist locals or real-life inspirations so those stories appear as characters in more films.

Will Poulter plays Cody, a man in a court-ordered recovery program in Union County. He’s doing fairly well in it until he reunites with his foster brother Jack (Noah Centineo). The film depicts both of their struggles to stay sober, while also highlighting these recovery programs and the people who use them. I first saw Union County at the Davis Theater in Chicago at a special screening with Poulter in attendance.

He explained his experiences with making the movie and having real people from Union County in it. You feel that community throughout. It, in a way, makes Union County feel more grounded in reality than other films with similar topics.

Addiction and recovery are popular subjects in art. Union County may be among the best films about addiction because it feels intimate and quiet while honestly and organically tackling addiction and recovery. Director Adam Meeks puts respect and care into the film’s authenticity and highlights the community without judgment.

I love hearing filmmakers, actors, and creatives speak about their work. You get a better understanding of the process and intentions behind things. You also get a firsthand look at the passion for the project. Therefore, I enjoyed hearing Poulter speak about the importance Meeks and he put into their work with the community. Someone in the audience at the Davis Theater showing knew a person who appeared in the film. She therefore further highlighted how the community bonded even more while making Union County.

Many actors carry the prejudgment that they don’t like working or associating with those outside the acting and filmmaking world. Therefore, it is refreshing to see and hear about those who care about working with all scene partners, whether they’re an extra or an Oscar-winning actor, with the same courtesy, respect, and compassion.

Union County digs into the many aspects of addiction, including mental health. It’s another very honest movie about the mental struggles of addiction. Effectively showcasing things like the mental health struggles of addiction likely comes from consulting those with addiction while creating this film.

Besides Poulter and Centineo’s brilliant performances, Union County gets a lot of its power and authenticity from the people in the community playing extras or small roles. They don’t feel like people playing a part but those putting their real life on the screen in one way or another. It’s these types of lived experiences that make movies such as Sing Sing and Union County unique but also profound.

Many movies are all about escapism, while others remind you of the tragedy and hope of everyday life. The latter films often stay with you longer. It’s more transformative when those who understand the experience of the characters personally participate in the making of movies.

Spent most of my life in various parts of Illinois, including attending college in Evanston. I have been a life long lover of pop culture, especially television, turned that passion into writing about all things entertainment related. When I'm not writing about pop culture, I can be found channeling Gordon Ramsay by kicking people out the kitchen.
