#3574. Shooting Suspect In Custody After Opening Fire Near Xbox Dev’s Studio

A drive-by shooting in Southern California ended with no injuries and an arrest after the gunman reportedly opened fire near a business and office campus that houses Xbox subsidiary InXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath and local affiliate KTLA5, the shooting occurred on November 11 at an office building on the former Marine Corps Air Station in Tustin, California. The police department posted on Facebook that, after uncovering "multiple shell casings in the area," local detectives worked "around the clock" to locate the suspect.

Sergeant Christopher Peterson told Aftermath on November 13 that although the investigation is still ongoing, an unnamed suspect had been apprehended "less than 48 hours" after the shooting.

"Officers got there [on November 11]," Sergeant Peterson said. "They responded to a report of a drive-by shooting there. Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt. Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why."

An InXile Entertainment spokesperson corroborated the incident with Aftermath, expressing relief about the situation.

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office,” the spokesperson said. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate."

Founded in 2002, InXile Entertainment has been under the Xbox Game Studios umbrella since 2018. Since its founding, the studio has developed several games, from the 2004 ARPG The Bard's Tale to the 2011 action-adventure Hunted: The Demon's Forge to the 2014 post-apocalyptic RPG Wasteland 2. Currently, the team is working on Clockwork Revolution, a steampunk ARPG not too dissimilar from immersive sims like BioShock and Dishonored. It has no release date right now, but InXile Entertainment is targeting a 2027 window for PC and Xbox Series X|S.

#3572. Firefox's New 'Mini Window' Feature Is a Game Changer for Productivity

David Nield is a technology journalist from Manchester in the U.K. who has been writing about gadgets and apps for more than 20 years.

He has a bachelor's degree in English Literature from Durham University, where he also spent a term as editor of the award-winning student newspaper Palatinate. His journalism career started in print media, where he contributed to and edited several technology magazines and bookazines sold in the U.K. and internationally. More recently, he has worked as a freelancer for some of the biggest technology publications on the web, covering everything from on-the-ground reporting about product launches, to detailed explainers and how-to guides on apps, gadgets, and platforms. His expertise covers broad areas of consumer tech, including smartphones, laptops, wearables, and AI.

For many of us, web browsing involves juggling dozens of tabs at once, and it's easy for important pages to get lost in the chaos. Now, Firefox has introduced something I think could help us multi-taskers: a "Mini Window." As highlighted by ZDNET's Jack Wallen, this new Firefox feature works like picture-in-picture overlays for videos—only here, that PiP displays a website.

"[Mini Window] lets you move a tab, or a selected section of a page, into a compact window that stays on top of your other windows while you browse," runs Mozilla's official blurb. "It's useful when you're multitasking and need to keep a few sources of information in view at once: Reference docs, a chat, a video call, a form you're filling out." As such, Mini Window doesn't necessarily replace running tabs side-by-side; rather, you can prioritize one tab in a full-size window, while keeping another page in view at all times.

This is a feature that's still in its early stages, and right now you can only get it in the "Nightly" version of Firefox, a very early beta version of the browser. Mozilla says it will push the feature to the full version of the browser later this month.

If you want to try this out as soon as possible, first install Firefox Nightly on your Mac or PC. Once up and running, you can launch Mini Window by right-clicking on a tab header and choosing Move Tab > Move to Mini Window. The tab shrinks and drops down to the lower right corner by default, staying on top of all other windows (not just Firefox). You can then scroll through the page and follow links as normal in the Mini Window—any links set to open in a new tab (manually or automatically) will launch in the main Firefox view, not the window overlay.

By dragging the title bar around, you can put your Mini Window anywhere you want on screen, and you can change its size by dragging the edges of the window too—so it doesn't necessarily have to be all that "mini." Firefox hides all buttons by default—including forward, backward, and refresh buttons, together with the address bar and buttons for closing the window or putting it back as a normal tab—though they appear when you hover over the Mini Window.

I'm finding the feature most useful when writing up articles where I need to refer to something else already on the web (so almost all of them), but there are a host of ways this can be used. It's particularly handy on a small laptop, where you don't necessarily have the screen space to put two tabs side by side, or when running a lower-priority window (like checking a social media site while reading an important document). No doubt, Firefox will continue to refine and improve the feature as it makes its way to the stable version of the browser, and it feels like something other browsers (looking at you, Google Chrome) might adopt as well in the near future. Eventually, using Mini Windows might become as common as opening up a long row of tabs.

We've gotten glimpses of Lithgow in the role of the Hogwarts Headmaster in previously released Harry Potter footage, but this new clip puts more emphasis on his mannerisms and I am loving it.

The clip opens with the newly sorted first years seated with the rest of their houses and chanting for Dumbledore. Once they're tucking into their feast, Dumbledore and Professor McGonagall have a chat about Harry being sorted into Gryffindor. "The cat that got the cream" is a clever idiom from the headmaster, when taking into account McGonagall's animagus abilities. For such a brief conversation, it really tells us a lot about the headmaster. He's playful and thoughtful all at once.

When Minerva comments on how much Harry looks like his father, Dumbledore's response is:

Looks can be deceiving, Minerva. His nature is entirely his own.

I love that Dumbledore isn't quick to assume Harry is everything like his father. McGonagall's tone is affectionate of course, but still softly suggests some expectation from the 11-year-old that Dumbledore seems quick to gently shut down. There are so many sides to Albus Dumbledore, and I love how this clip shows Lithgow grasping more than one of them.

Beyond Lithgow's words in this scene, there's also his mannerisms. Before he sits down, Dumbledore snaps his fingers to prompt the food to appear on the tables. Then, when it's time for dessert, I'm assuming that little flourish of his fork as he's about to grab some meat, is the prompt to turn dinner service into dessert for the kids. It's little details like that that I can't wait to see more of.

On the less positive side, I'm not entirely sure I love the way the food appeared. There was something slightly off -- or maybe slightly too perfect? -- about the way the food snapped into reality that bugged me. I'm trying to keep an open mind as we see more magic in use in this series, and it's possible my brain is just too familiar with the sight of the plates appearing in the movie -- which is admittedly a wide shot from very far away before we see the food close up -- to accept this new version quite yet. (Considering some of the food featured in the movie had apparently spoiled after sitting out for days of filming, maybe I shouldn't cling so much to memories that scene.)

I will say that when the dessert appeared, my brain flashed back to that scene in Hook when Peter finally sees all the food at the table. Dumbledore may have conjured dessert for the students, but he conjured instant childhood memories over here, and my stomach growled.

We're a little more than a month out from the premiere of Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone. It seems likely that HBO will give us another glimpse or two between now and then, but nothing will compare to sitting down for the first episode when it debuts on Christmas. Between what we know and love from the books and scenes that weren't straight from the page, there will be a lot to dive into as Season 1 gets going.

#3570. NBA 2K27’s GTA 6 Crossover Includes A Whole GTA-Inspired Limited Edition Of The Game

Ahead of the GTA 6 release this week, publisher Take-Two Interactive and 2K Sports have announced an NBA 2K27 crossover with the game. Starting November 27, Vice City will take over the digital basketball courts, and a special-edition NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition will also be released to promote GTA 6.

The $80 digital-only NBA 2K27 Vice City Edition features Miami Heat player Bam Adebayo on the cover, and for that GTA 6 touch, the art also includes the signature Vice City neon glow. This is something of a first for Take-Two Interactive--and possibly, the rest of the industry--as releasing a special edition of a game that promotes another game isn't something that we've seen before. This version also includes bonus Vice City-themed content and several benefits for GTA+ subscribers.

For Season 3 of NBA 2K27's live-service league, Vice City-themed content and rewards across The City social hub and MyTeam mode will be available to unlock. This three-week promotion will include bonuses and access for GTA+ Members, and Take-Two says players can expect themed apparel, including Vice City and Los Santos jerseys, Burger Shot and Cluckin' Bell Employee Outfits, and more.

Vice City-themed limited-time events will run throughout the season, with players competing in Conquer Leonida and Vice Run. Wednesdays will offer a chance to earn extra reputation by wearing Rockstar Games collaboration gear in Wear & Earn events, and one of the new modes is Neon vs. Noir, a 5v5 full-court clash pitting a Vice City team against a Los Santos lineup. MyTeam will also feature Vice City-themed cards, a powerful new Premier Exchange card, and limited-time modes.

The new gear will cost you some bucks, as the Season 3 Pro Pass--which offers access to the premium track with Vice City rewards like the Burger Shot gear, Cluckin' Bell outfit, Cactus Jack jersey, and Macca the Gator--will cost $10. The Hall of Fame Pass, which includes everything from the Pro Pass, 10 instant Level Skips, an extra 15% XP booster, and 15,000 VC, is priced at $20, and to get all the GTA-themed cosmetics, you have to grind through the 40-level season track. If you purchase the Vice City edition, the Season 3 Pro Pass is bundled with your copy.

GTA+ members on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S can also play the standard edition of NBA 2K27 for free from November 27 to January 15, 2027. If they like what they see, they'll get 20% off the game if they choose to purchase. GTA 6 preorders also include a one-month trial of GTA+.

Finally, GTA+ members can also download a Vice City bonus content pack featuring a Vice City-styled blue boat hat and oversized T-shirt, 30 skill boosts for five games, and 15 Gatorade boosts for five games.

GTA 6 marketing has been heating up as the game gets closer to launch, and this isn't the only basketball promotion on the table. For one night only, the NBA's Miami Heat will wear GTA 6-inspired jerseys when they host the Milwaukee Bucks on November 18, and the match will take place on a court inspired by Vice City.

#3569. These Signature Sony Headphones Are Under $200 Ahead of Black Friday

The Sony WH-1000XM6 headphones are the most recent entry in Sony's 1000X series, which has been around since 2016. They're the best over-ear headphones in terms of audio quality currently on the market—but not everyone can (or needs to) drop nearly half a grand on headphones.

The WH-1000XM5 are a generation older and were at the top of their class until they were supplanted by the XM6. On the plus side, by virtue of being older, they're currently discounted to $198 (down from the original $399.99) during Amazon's early Black Friday sale. That 50% off brings it down to the lowest price they've ever reached, a good deal for premium headphones that still sound incredible, even in 2026.

I have been a loyal customer of the 1000X line for many years; they're my go-to headphones for most activities. The WH-1000XM5 received an "outstanding" review from PCMag for their top-notch audio quality and exceptional audio when using the best-in-class active noise cancellation. The headphones are also well-designed to be comfortable for long listening sessions. The ear controls use tapping and swiping, which isn't my favorite, but it's what all modern headphones are moving toward. There's a companion app that lets you adjust your EQ settings to your liking, including what the swiping and tapping functions do.

These headphones also have a stereo 3.5mm connection, which is perfect for those who want to use a cable and not worry about battery life. And speaking of battery life, Sony says you can expect about 30 hours, but it will vary depending on your use of ANC. They are compatible with AAC, LDAC, and SBC codecs and have multipoint connection, meaning you can pair them with more than one device at the same time.

Personally, I think the value for the money you get with the XM5 for $198 is better than paying full price for the XM6. If you're looking to get ahead of the Black Friday chaos and secure an amazing deal on great headphones, this is it.

#3567. Rockstar Could Have Released GTA 6 Sooner As GTA 5.5, But “You Have To Take Big Swings”

After years of development, multiple delays, and loads of hype, Rockstar Games is finally releasing Grand Theft Auto 6 on November 19. What took so long?

According to Rockstar publishing executive Jennifer Kolbe, the team at Rockstar "could have made GTA 5.5, and done it faster." However, "Ultimately, that's not what they wanted," she told The Guardian.

Rockstar boss Rob Nelson, meanwhile, said it was important for the studio to go above and beyond with GTA 6, and that takes time. "You have to take big swings. It can’t be just more of the same," he said.

GTA 6 looks to be a big step up from GTA 5 in a number of ways, including the visuals and technical improvements. Beyond that, the story this time around is a Bonnie-and-Clyde-style narrative about a crime-loving couple--Jason and Lucia. It's also the first time Rockstar is releasing a GTA game with a playable female protagonist.

GTA 6 took so long to come out because Rockstar is seeking "perfection," according to Take-Two. “The team at Rockstar really does seek to do something that’s never been done before. That’s really hard and it takes a long time,” he said.

Rockstar and its owner, Take-Two, stand to benefit greatly from what's expected to be a commercial blockbuster with GTA 6. But could future GTA game releases come at a faster pace? According to Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, the "nature and velocity" of GTA releases will look "dramatically different" over the next decade, but he didn't share more or commit to any specific timelines.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. People in Australia can attend a funeral at KFC to get the day off work to play it.

GTA 6 unlocks at midnight local time and not simultaneously around the world. This means people in the US will be among the last in the world to get to play.

#3566. As Hollywood Battles AI, Pedro Pascal Says Making Behemoth! Filled Him with “a Tremendous Amount of Hope”

Pedro Pascal says that the character he plays in Behemoth!, his first leading film role, is the “closest thing to me that I’ve ever done.” And because of this, “the experience on set felt surreal in a sort of physically tangible way,” Pascal told the audience during a Q&A at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday.

Directed by Tony Gilroy, Behemoth! tells the story of Alex, a prodigal cellist who returns to Los Angeles and the world of Hollywood film scoring after decades performing symphonic work around the country.

“The mixing of my own life and this person's life, I've lived a very nomadic one. Don't ask me where home is. And so that felt like it was crossing personal lines for me in a way,” he continued during a post-screening discussion about the film, which featured Pascal and writer-director Tony Gilroy, moderated by VF's West Coast Editor John Ross.

Tony Gilroy and Pedro Pascal  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

But according to Gilroy, their collaboration on the film almost didn't happen, thanks to an alleged missed connection at a Star Wars event.

“We went to a Star Wars convention in Tokyo where we took Andor,” recalled Gilroy. “There was this big Disney dinner so all the Star Wars people are there and [Pascal] was kind of busy and flighty.”

“I had the flu! I flew from London to Tokyo!” Pascal countered.

Gilroy continued: “He seemed like he was so hip that he didn't come to the dinner. I thought, 'Oh he's got such a great thing going on he's going to some better party; he's not going to a boring dinner.'”

As the audience laughed, Pascal was quick to set the record straight: “I cannot believe that you thought that I ditched that dinner. I was doing re-shoots of Fantastic Four!” he said. “They flew me to Tokyo that night and flew me back and I was on a set. [Turns toward the audience] Can you believe this?”

“Oh my God. I'm calling Kathy Kennedy [the President of Lucasfilm] right away,” Gilroy joked.

Luckily, the moviemaking stars (and schedules) aligned and the pair was able to make their personal, moving film with Pascal serving as Gilroy's “exclamation point. He has all the sadness and all the covering that this character needs to have and the nomadic life.”

Pedro Pascal, Tony Gilroy and John Ross at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal and Gilroy formed a genuine bond and are very comfortable making playful jabs at each other, keeping things light but also expressing their gratitude for being able to make Behemoth! their way, in Los Angeles, where the film and television industry has been struggling to regain a foothold. Despite the challenges, past and present, they are holding out hope for human-made storytelling to foster further human connection.

“People's natural resistance to the robot takeover is clear,” said Gilroy when asked about the rise of AI. “I don't know what's going to happen. I really don't. The music scene out here is the coral reef of what's happened. It's been dying out here for the last 15 years… It's grooving a little bit now. I think people want humans. I don't know what's going to come back, but this is this incredibly humanizing element of movies that's happened. Can it be replaced by AI? Probably, quite shockingly, simply. There's probably an emotional amplitude knob on some f—ing algorithm, but this movie is organic.”

Pedro Pascal and Tony Gilroy  at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Pascal walked away from Behemoth! feeling optimistic. “The experience of shooting this movie definitely injected me with a tremendous amount of hope,” he said. “We weren't making money on this movie. Nobody was. And you had the most expensive people involved in this film because of their talent and their experience. So there was just this purity of love in the work from every single department, and that was incredibly contagious. And it was primarily locations, and so Los Angeles was just constantly revealing itself in all of these magical ways because we were so location-based. I had shot a series in Colombia for three seasons, and I would argue that the primary character of that series, Narcos, was shooting it in the country of Colombia because there was only one way of capturing that energy and that physical story. And LA did that as well. And then it's so tender. I think the story is incredibly tender. Would you ever expect it from this guy [gestures to Gilroy]?”

“Oh my God. What a cold, weird thing to say,” the director joked.

“There are other movies this year that I think in their own way, movies that I've seen this year that I love so much, that fight for humanity and the storytelling,” Pascal continued. “So I think that there is a sort of pushback that could be really, really thrilling as far as [creativity] is concerned, as far as politics is concerned. We want to be human beings and we want to be connected to one another and we want to tell each other's stories and witness each other's stories and we want to look after each other and all that shit. That's my hope.”

Tony Gilroy at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Gilroy had another suggestion: “Blow up the AI centers, man," he joked. “I don't mean to blow them up. I mean blow them up at the voting box. Go and vote and blow them up. Go see the Musk documentary, man. Go see that, watch the whole four hours. I'm pitching my movie [here], but watch that movie.”

The invitation-only events are welcoming an audience from the worlds of film, fashion, culture, politics, media, and tech, much like the magazine itself.

Following the program in Los Angeles, Vanity Fair’s Screening Room will arrive in New York, where screenings and events will take place at Cherry Lane Theatre from December 4–6.

#3565. Five Hacks Every Una Watch User Should Know

The Una watch is pretty much made to be hackable, with its interchangeable parts and open development environment. But it’s also pretty barebones at launch, without many features available yet. However, here are five things I’ve discovered I can do with it—and I hope to expand this list quite a bit as the device and its community mature.

Because the Una watch has a regular USB-C port, you don’t need to remember any specific cable, dongle, or adapter to charge it. I knew that, but it didn’t occur to me until recently that I didn’t need a computer or a wall outlet to plug into the other end. I was able to take a USB-C to USB-C cable—the same kind I might carry around to charge my phone—and plug one end into my watch and the other into my phone. It charged!

(You can also charge some other devices from a phone, including an Apple Watch, but you’d need to carry around that specific adapter, which is why nobody bothers.)

The Una watch doesn’t have any built-in sleep tracking, but a few community-built apps aim to provide it. The Slumber app, for example, will let you know how long you slept and compare your most recent bedtime with when you usually get to bed. There are no sleep stages (honestly: refreshing, since watches are rarely good at this anyway), and the analysis is done on the watch itself.

But if what you’re really hoping for is a recovery score or an overnight HRV reading, the HabitLab app combines that with habit tracking. Every evening, the watch will buzz and ask you to check off which habits or factors played into your day: Alcohol and late meals are among the options, and the watch will automatically detect morning or evening workouts to add them to the list. In the morning, the watch asks you how you slept, and then it gives you a score based on your resting heart rate, HRV, and your subjective rating.

The app is supposed to be able to put together trends and insights from this data, but I haven’t managed to get it to do this. Maybe it’s waiting for more data (I’ve been using it a little over a week), or maybe it’s just buggy.

By contrast, the barcode app worked even better than I expected it to. It’s meant for a parkrun barcode; each participant in the free weekly 5K has a number that you can use to check your results online. But it works just as well for other barcodes.

I installed the Barcode app and entered the number for my library card. Perhaps because of the watch’s MIP screen, I found this barcode scanned more reliably than any barcodes I’ve previously tried to use on a watch. The library scanner picked it up just fine on the first try, and a phone-based scanner also had no problem with it. You can store up to six barcodes, so I’ve also entered a few others, like my grocery discount card.

The app supports QR codes as well as regular barcodes, and to enter a QR code, you just type in a shortened URL. (It needs to be 22 characters or less.) This means that the Barcode app is also a QR code creator, a nifty feature indeed.

Seeing how soon the sun sets is a bit of a downer as we leave daylight saving time and get into the dark winter months, but it’s also helpful in planning. The Sun & Moon Face puts a graphic on your wrist that shows how far along the sun is in its trajectory across the sky for the day. When evening is approaching, you’ll see just how little time you have left.

The app grabs your GPS location once a day, which means that for the first few hours I wore it, the sunrise and sunset times were incorrectly listed as 6 a.m. and 6 p.m. But as long as you aren’t flying to a drastically new location every day, the app does the job just fine. As a bonus, it changes the color of the screen’s sky to show daylight, nighttime, or sunrise/sunset colors.

If you want to hack this hackable watch, you might as well take the plunge and try to build something yourself. Instructions are here to download the development tools for Windows, Mac, or Linux, and there are tutorials for different features you might want to use and implement. There are also about a dozen example apps you can build on, including activity trackers, watch faces, and glances. I'm not much of a coder myself, but this is the friendliest setup I've seen for someone to get into building their own apps for a watch.

#3564. EA Begs You To Not Delete Madden 27 For GTA 6

We all know what's coming: Grand Theft Auto 6. Whether you're ready for it or not, the most anticipated game of the decade is preparing to launch on November 19, and ahead of its release, EA is begging you to please not ditch footballs for guns.

According to Push Square, EA added a "don't delete" pop-up message to Madden NFL 27. The pop-up says there's an update coming to the football simulator on November 17, just before GTA 6 drops.

"Don't delete," the message reads. "[Encrypted Signal] The target is locked. The crew is assembling for a high-stakes run. Await the signal from our insider on 11/17 ... do not leak this transmission!"

In a November 10 post on Madden NFL 27's official X account, EA said that a throwback Madden 97 update is coming on November 18 with old-school playbooks, 16-bit gameplay, and the All '97 Team. Underneath that post, EA had asked that you stick around a little while longer.

This is in reference to the humongous amount of storage space that Rockstar Games' GTA 6 will take up when it launches. Start clearing out your hard drive now because you need at least 212GB of free space to download GTA 6. In comparison, Madden NFL 27 needs approximately 60GB to install the game.

If you're like me and you still have the base PS5, this means you have approximately 667GB of usable space. Sure, you can fit both GTA 6 and Madden NFL 27 on the same console. However, if you have any other recent releases like The Blood of Dawnwalker (~50GB), Dragon's Dogma 2: Dark Arisen (~81GB), Phantom Blade Zero (~135GB), and Valor Mortis (~60GB), then you can see how quickly you'll run out of space--especially since you have to leave a little wiggle room for game updates, too. That's not to mention the games dropping in 2027, such as Final Fantasy VII Revelation, which game director Naoki Hamaguchi said could be around 200GB.

EA has recently gone through a restructuring that saw 400 employees across the company get let go and the legendary studio BioWare get shut down. In the midst of this, the publisher reiterated its commitment to the Madden franchise with a new title currently codenamed Project Gridiron. While filled with potential, we do fear that EA's plan for the series may lean into everything that the company itself does wrong.

Spoilers ahead about the most recent episode of The Great British Baking Show.

I love reality TV, although most of the shows I watch are cutthroat like Survivor, The Traitors, or the Real Housewives. I decided to watch The Great British Baking Show for the first time this year with my Netflix subscription, and have loved how charming and wholesome the series is in comparison. As such, I was surprised when the latest episode legit made me cry, largely thanks to how much Moyin was crying over Connie's elimination. Luckily there is a silver lining with this heartbreak.

Bake Off has been a joy to watch, from Nigella Lawson's passion for eating to the kindness the contestants extend to each other. Last week's Pastry Week had my mouth watering, but for Caramel Week it was my eyes that was producing the moisture. I was left in a puddle by the time the latest episode ended, but luckily the franchise cheered me up thanks to some delightful content of their reunion. Case in point: the following video from Bake Off's official Instagram account. Check it out for yourself below.

A post shared by The Great British Bake Off (@britishbakeoff)

I mean, how adorable are these two? Clearly their bond extends outside of the Bake Off tent, and they've remained close in the time between filming and the current season airing. It would have been heartwarming enough to merely see Connie and Moyin reuniting, but the fact that they showed off their dance moves in the above video is even more delightful. So while the latest episode of The Great British Baking Show made me cry, I'm back to enjoying the show's immense charm.

From the premiere of Bake Off's season, it seemed like the cooling process was going to be a challenge for the bakers in the midst of a heat wave across the pond. That proved challenging for Connie during Caramel Week, and after fumbling both the Signature and Showstopper, Connie was ultimately eliminated. Cue the tears.

New episodes of The Great British Baking Show air Fridays on Netflix as part of the 2026 TV schedule. We'll just have to see if the remainder of the season makes me cry again, or if it'll stay charming and wholesome.

#3562. GTA 6 Should Help Boost PS5 And Xbox Sales, But Their Astronomical Prices Could Hurt

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 launches on November 19, and it's expected to help boost console sales for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. But the uptick in hardware sales might not be as dramatic as you might think--and there is a good reason why.

According to Circana's Mat Piscatella, there will be "probably" be a boost to PS5 and Xbox Series X|S sales when GTA 6 comes out, but the uptick could be muted due to the recent PS5 and Xbox Series X|S price hikes. Piscatella said anyone who is excited for GTA 6 and needs a new console might think twice when they see how astronomically expensive new consoles have become today.

Historical prices

When GTA 5 launched in 2013, the average price paid for a new PS3 was $252 and the Xbox 360 was $232. Adjusted for inflation, that would be $363 for the PS3 today and $334 for the Xbox 360. Those prices are significantly below the average price of a new PS5 ($646) and Xbox Series X|S ($663) today.

"Not a good thing"

Earlier this year, Take-Two boss Strauss Zelnick, who oversees the company launching GTA 6, said, "The rising cost of hardware is not a good thing." At the same time, Zelnick isn't worried about the impact on GTA 6, in part because he believes the game is so good that people will find a way to pay for a new console.

 "However, a lower price point for hardware would be a good thing because there’d be more hardware in people’s hands," he said. "Probably the most relevant thing is the world continues to move to open systems, and that will continue.”

#3561. High School Teacher Arrested for Allegedly Planning to Have Sex With Girl, 15

A high school teacher in Pennsylvania was arrested after he allegedly made arrangements online to have sex with a 15-year-old girl, who was actually an undercover officer.

Fayette County District Attorney Michael Aubele said that Lester Eugene Everly II allegedly arranged to meet up and pay for sex during an online conversation with an officer, whom he believed was an adult offering him the opportunity to have sex with a 15-year-old girl they knew, according to WTAE.

Aubele went on to explain how they caught Everly, 47, in the act.

“Our police officer was posing as a person who had a girlfriend who had a 15-year-old child that he could make available for $170,” Aubele said in a statement. “So the defendant traveled to this location, South Union Township, brought other things that he was asked to bring with him, that he would need for sexual activity. We were able to confirm that this was the individual that we believed we were speaking to online.”

Everly was arrested on Saturday, November 14, as part of the undercover operation that the Pennsylvania State Police Uniontown Criminal Investigation Unit and the PSP Bureau of Criminal Investigation Computer Crime Unit ran together.

After Everly was taken into custody, police said he confessed to bringing a condom and $180 to the meetup location he previously arranged with the officer.

Everly is currently in custody at Fayette County Prison. His preliminary hearing is scheduled to take place on November 23.

In light of the scandal, Everly has been identified as a teacher at Albert Gallatin High School in Fayette County, Pennsylvania.

Following Everly’s arrest, Albert Gallatin Interim Superintendent Dr. Jason Hutchinson issued a statement regarding the citation.

“Albert Gallatin has been informed of the arrest of a staff member last evening. The safety and security of our students is always the District’s primary concern, and will be the District’s focus as this matter proceeds,” Hutchinson said, per the outlet. “The District is cooperating with law enforcement and is unable to comment further.”

It’s not currently clear whether Everly has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The Pennsylvania State Police did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment when contacted about updates in the case.

#3559. Kate Middleton Announces First Major Trip Since Her Cancer Diagnosis

In unexpected news, Kensington Palace has just announced that Kate Middleton will accompany Prince William on his upcoming three-day official visit to Mumbai, India. The trip, which commences on Monday, will mark their first joint tour outside the United Kingdom in the past four years and represents a new milestone in Kate Middleton’s gradual return to public duties since she was diagnosed with cancer in early 2024 and began scaling back her official engagements.

Last May, the princess made a brief solo trip to Italy to learn about early childhood development, but this trip to India (a nine-hour flight from London) represents her first long-distance journey and her highest-profile diplomatic engagement since the Caribbean tour she undertook in 2022 and the Earthshot Awards gala she attended in Boston that same year.

"So proud, I'm very, very proud. She's been amazing. She's been through so much in the last couple of years, particularly," William shared on UK radio show Heart Breakfast in May, pleased to see that Kate was “gradually resuming” her travels. Still, the heir to the throne wanted to be cautious and warned that these visits are very taxing. "Away trips like that take a lot out of you," he explained. "So we have to balance that, make sure she's, she's OK and rested, but she's in good form."

The royal couple at the 2022 Earthshot Prize ceremony in Boston, their most recent joint trip abroad to date

The reason for the visit is the sixth edition of the Earthshot Prize, an initiative spearheaded by the heir to the British throne that each year awards one million pounds (about $1,323,249) to five innovative environmental projects and which, after making stops in other cities abroad such as Singapore, Cape Town, and Rio de Janeiro, is now taking place in the country that has produced the most finalists and winners in the competition’s history.

Standout finalists this year include Mahindra Last Mile Mobility, for its fleet of electric motorcycle taxis designed to reduce urban pollution, and Mahila Housing Trust, which installs reflective roofs capable of lowering the temperature inside homes by up to five degrees during extreme heat. The awards ceremony will be held this Tuesday evening at the Jio World Centre in Mumbai and will feature a performance by the band Take That and be attended by celebrities such as actor Rami Malek.

William and Kate during their 2016 visit to the Taj Mahal

Hours before the main event, the Prince and Princess of Wales will also preside over the first edition of the Earthshot Children’s Awards, a competition in which 15,000 schools from 24 Indian states have participated with environmental proposals designed by young people aged 9 to 17. The itinerary also includes a solo appearance by Kate Middleton, meetings with the Bollywood film industry, cricket-related celebrations, and a possible meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

In addition to being a positive sign regarding the princess’s health, this return to India holds strong symbolic significance for the couple, who last visited the country in April 2016. On that occasion, the then-Duke and Duchess of Cambridge visited the Taj Mahal and posed on the same white marble bench where Princess Diana was photographed alone in 1992—an image that has gone down in history as a reflection of the breakdown of her marriage to the now-King Charles III.

#3558. WoW: Forever’s Dungeons Have Gotten Yet Another Big Change

World of Warcraft: Forever's dungeons have changed once again, with developer Blizzard's most recent adjustment requiring an emergency hotfix to address players' outcry.

Dungeons, specifically how much experience points players earn from them, have been one of Forever's most debated topics going back to the game's beta. Make them too lucrative, and players will just stay inside dungeons instead of questing out in the world. At the same time, Blizzard doesn't want dungeons to be one-time affairs, with players completing all their quests in a single run and never going back.

Blizzard opened a new front in the dungeon wars on November 13, making a change so that nobody in a dungeon group would receive any experience if enemies were considered "trivial" to to any player in the group. The idea behind this appeared to be an effort to prevent high-level players from running low-level ones through dungeons, in the process curtailing players from selling character "boosting" services to lowbies.

Unfortunately, far too many players playing the game normally were caught in the crossfire. Many of Forever's dungeons have double-digit level ranges, meaning even if a player might find enemies early on in the dungeon trivial, enemies and bosses later on won't be. It also created a scenario where players were leveling up mid-dungeon, only to suddenly find themselves fighting trivial enemies and bricking the experience gains for everyone in the group.

As it turns out, committing to a multi-hour adventure, only to suddenly find nobody is earning experience points and everyone is mad at you because you happened to level up, is not a great social experience. Blizzard was at least quick to admit the change "missed the mark" and made adjustments a day later on November 14.

"With hotfixes that are now live, we've just deployed a further change to this restriction, making it so the XP nullification only kicks in when the high-level player is more than 12 levels above the level of the enemies," Blizzard said in a forum post. 

At least judging from forum comments, that seems to be a more reasonable compromise, even if it still does prevent higher-level players from coming to help their lower-level friends.

It's just the latest chapter in what has become one of the biggest ongoing discussions in the Forever community. During the Forever beta, Blizzard made changes to experience earned from dungeon quests, nerfing them significantly. 

Come launch day, it became apparent Forever's dungeons weren't worth running more than once, as after completing quests, experience earned from kills was extremely low. Blizzard agreed, and issued a change on November 8 to increase the amount of kill experience earned in dungeons by 50%. It was a sizable increase, but is still lower than the experience amount players earned from doing dungeons in WoW Classic.

Forever's launch broke WoW concurrent-player records, and after one week of adventuring through Azeroth once more, classic WoW feels fresh again. Despite the record-breaking launch, Blizzard hasn't released official stats, but fansites have already pieced together the game's most popular class, race, and faction.

I thought I'd made peace with saying goodbye to James Gunn's Guardians of the Galaxy. The third movie wrapped things up beautifully, and with Gunn running DC Studios, I figured there wasn't much chance of getting the old gang back together. Well, Hollywood has a funny way of changing plans. Gunn is leaving his leadership position at DC, and Chris Pratt is already talking about the possibility of making another Guardians movie with him. Let me just state for the record that I'm right there with him.

With Avengers: Doomsday approaching on the 2026 movie schedule, Pratt's future as Star-Lord has been on my mind lately. During a recent interview with MovieZine while promoting Way of the Warrior Kid, the actor was asked whether he'd be interested in reuniting with Gunn for a fourth installment. He hadn't spoken to the filmmaker since the DC news broke, but his answer was encouraging:

He directed all three movies, and that's pretty rare… so if he wanted to come back and bring it back, I would love that.

Well, now I want it too. Gunn spent nearly a decade building one of Marvel's strangest superhero teams into something audiences genuinely cared about. Somehow, he also made me cry over a talking raccoon more times than I'd care to admit.

This conversation is considerably less cheerful for DC fans. Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-heads of DC Studios following the Warner Bros. ownership shake-up, with former Marvel executive Jeremy Latcham taking over Dec. 1, raising plenty of questions about the DC Universe's future.

Gunn isn't exactly sitting at home waiting for Marvel to call. He's still involved with Man of Tomorrow, his follow-up to 2025's Superman, which is scheduled for July 2027. He also has other DC-related work on his plate. Still, stepping away from running an entire studio should eventually give him more freedom to choose what he wants to direct. But does he want to direct a fourth GotG?

Pratt's comments are especially interesting because he previously had some pretty specific thoughts about returning as Star-Lord. Last year, I covered his concerns about finding somebody who could fill Gunn's shoes. At the time, it seemed unlikely the filmmaker would ever be available. Suddenly, that possibility doesn't sound quite so ridiculous.

There's also the matter of where we left Peter Quill. At the end of Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3, he returned to Earth to reconnect with his grandfather, while Rocket took charge of a new Guardians lineup. The movie's closing credits promised Star-Lord would return, though the powers that be haven't said in what capacity or which new Marvel flick he might show up in.

Pratt recently confirmed there have been conversations about bringing him back, which is encouraging. Although returning for another Avengers movie and reuniting with Gunn for a fourth Guardians adventure would be two very different things. There's still no indication that Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 4 is actually happening. Gunn spent years saying the third movie would conclude his trilogy, and he may have no interest in revisiting those characters. I certainly wouldn't blame him for wanting to move on from comic book and superhero fare to something completely different. At this point, he's been helming superhero content for more than a decade. Maybe he wants to spread his wings and take on a different type of movie, which I would be stoked for as well.

Still, I love the idea of Pratt and Gunn finding their way back to each other, especially after everything they accomplished with the first three movies. Maybe it's wishful thinking, but if Gunn ever decides he's ready for another trip into space, I hope Marvel answers the phone.

The first three original Guardians of the Galaxy films are available to stream with a Disney+ subscription.

#3556. The Head Of GTA 6’s Parent Company Helped Make One Of The Best Christmas Movies Of All Time

One of the most memorable and beloved Christmas movies is 1990's Home Alone, but it almost didn't happen, and the head of GTA 6's parent company played a role in bringing the movie to market.

Strauss Zelnick, the current CEO of Rockstar Games owner Take-Two, was the president and COO of 20th Century Fox at the time--he was among the youngest-ever Hollywood CEOs at the age of 32.

Warner Bros. was originally backing Home Alone and had actually begun production on the movie until budget concerns prompted the studio to pull the plug. "Four days into production, they shut down the picture and canceled it. That never happens," Zelnick told David Rubenstein.

Fox, under the leadership of chairman Joe Roth and Zelnick as president, swooped in and gave the filmmakers--including director Christopher Columbus and writer John Hughes--the money to make Home Alone.

That turned out to be a fantastic investment for Fox, as Home Alone ranked as one of the top five highest-grossing movies of the year in the US. It grossed more than $476 million globally against a $13 million budget, and it picked up two Oscar nominations. Home Alone also helped launch the career of Macaulay Culkin, and his role of Kevin remains his most memorable part.

So why didn't Zelnick keep making movies?

Zelnick was on top of the world as a film executive after Home Alone. However, he said he saw a bright future in the interactive entertainment business, so he left Fox in 1993 to join Crystal Dynamics where he served as president and CEO.

"I left Fox voluntarily, which no one ever does, to move to Silicon Valley, take a 95% pay cut and become the pre-revenue CEO of a little tiny video game company called Crystal Dynamics in 1993," he said in the Rubenstein interview.

After Crystal Dynamics, Zelnick shifted to the music business in the role of CEO as BMG Entertainment from 1994 to 2000. During that time, BMG started a gaming unit, BMG Interactive, which published the original GTA in 1997.

After that, Zelnick and an investor group took over Take-Two, which was in a tough financial spot at the time and was sued by the US government for accounting fraud.

Since the takeover, Take-Two has thrived. Its share price exploded from about $10 in 2007 to more than $220 today, and Take-Two today has a market cap of over $40 billion. The GTA franchise is a juggernaut at Take-Two, but it actually only accounts for 15% of the company's revenue in a non-release quarter. Take-Two today owns and operates a number of big non-GTA franchises, including NBA 2K, Borderlands, Mafia, BioShock, Civilization, and more.

GTA 6 launches on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. It's reportedly already sold close to 15 million copies and generated nearly $1.5 billion in revenue.

#3554. This TP-Link Wi-Fi 7 Travel Router Is 27% Off for This Early Black Friday Deal

Pradershika Sharma is a tech deals writer for Lifehacker. She has a Master’s degree in English Literature, a B.Ed., and a TESOL certification. She has been writing professionally since 2018, creating product reviews, affiliate articles, and search ads for global clients while working with Rubix Agency and Cognizant. Previously, she spent a year teaching English at the junior high level.An avid reader since childhood, Pradershika's idea of extreme sports is staying up to read “just one more chapter.” She lives in India.

A novel solution for connecting to the internet on the go, the TP-Link Roam 7 travel router is now down to $87.99 from $119.99 in an early Black Friday deal—marking its lowest price to date. This is not a full-size home router but, as the name suggests, a compact travel companion that measures roughly the size of a paperback book, with foldable antennas so it slips easily into a bag.

More about convenience than chasing top speeds, you can use the Roam 7 as a standard router, connect it to public wifi to create a private network, or share your phone's internet through USB tethering. It also supports Ethernet input and USB modems, along with range extender and wireless client modes. That flexibility is particularly useful when you’re juggling a laptop, phone, and maybe a tablet and would prefer not to sign each one into a shaky network separately. Setup is straightforward through the TP-Link Tether app: scan a QR code, choose your connection type, and you’re online in a few minutes.

Once it’s running, the hardware covers the basics, with a 2.5 Gbps port for a wired connection like a hotel’s Ethernet jack, a 1 Gbps port for a wired device, and a USB 3.0 port for a storage drive or phone tethering. And since it draws power over USB-C (5V/3A), a basic power bank can keep it going through a long layover or a camping trip. As handy as it is on the road, though, it’s not meant to replace a full-size home router—even with its 5 GHz band and Wi-Fi 7 support—which will generally offer better coverage and more consistent speeds. Real-world performance also depends heavily on your connection and setup. USB tethering, for example, can feel slower than using your phone directly. It also leaves out features like automatic band steering, so you may end up managing networks yourself. Still, if you travel often or need a portable network hub for multiple devices, you’ll find it holds up pretty well.

#3553. Sam Altman Is “Still Unknowable” to Andrew Garfield, Even After Playing the OpenAI Co-Founder in Artificial

In Luca Guadagnino’s Artificial, the director follows the rise of OpenAI and a few of its pioneers: Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Ilya Sutskever and Mira Murati. The result is one of the most talked-about and timely films of the season.

“The topic is not the artificial intelligence for me, but it's the people who imagined it, who created it, who exploited it and who are still in the mix of doing all these things,” Guadagnino said during a discussion led by VF's Global Editorial Director Mark Guiducci, at Vanity Fair’s Screening Room at LACMA on Saturday. “I was very much into trying to decipher, understand this world of this new generation, let’s say tech bros, that were somehow behaving in a way that was not exactly as you could see the previous generation doing … So it was too attractive not to try to meet these people in the eyes and too attractive not to do so with this incredible group of performers who were going to go and jump the cliff of this.”

Luca Guadagnino and Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Guadagnino was joined by cast members Andrew Garfield (who plays Altman), Yura Borisov (who plays Sutskever) and Monica Barbaro (who plays Murati) for a post-screening conversation. The actors were challenged with preparing to play real people who they were not able to interact with ahead of time, instead relying on interviews, video recordings, and other research in order to get into their characters.

Andrew Garfield at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

“[Sam Altman] still is unknowable to me and I'm fascinated by him continuously and exponentially, for here until eternity," Garfield said about OpenAI's co-founder and CEO. “And it's important to try to understand because as Luca said, these are the kids that have the reins of the future and we've somehow allowed them to just hold onto them. And we've kind of given our autonomy over or it's been taken from behind our backs.”

He added: “It's a remarkable thing to have the resilience to go and sleep every night, knowing that you're really doing a lot of damage.”

Barbaro said the fact that Murati is very private helped her understand the former OpenAI CTO. “That is indicative of a kind of behavior and personality type and it pointed me in a certain direction as far as her values were concerned,” she said. “And we also had a lot of wonderful consultants, people who worked with them at OpenAI, but who were no longer with the company, kind of telling us what jokes and things that they would make.”

Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

For Borisov, he hopes his portrayal does Sutskever justice and that people will want to know or understand him more. “I started to watch videos about him and looked at his social media, trying just to understand what he's talking about in his interviews,” the actor explained. "And step by step, as much as I discovered him, it was more and more scary for me because I started to respect and love him more and more."

Monica Barbaro, Andrew Garfield and Yura Borisov at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

The conversation had its own meta moment of sorts, when Barbaro posed a question to Guiducci about his decision to profile and feature Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair’s New Establishment Issue.

"You faced heat for presenting, maybe some people would say pedestalizing Sam Altman on the cover of Vanity Fair, what is your take on that?" Barbaro asked.

“I think that the magazine is an arena where these things have to play out,” Guiducci said. “It's so interesting to me to...have the [forthcoming] feature about this film in the issue that was preceded by one where I got to ask Sam about it." Guiducci continued: "Something about [taking Sam's] picture makes people feel, ‘Oh, that's the trophy.’ But photojournalism is journalism too. And I want people to be able to look back at the magazine and see a document of the time that we lived in," he said. "And also, if the photo is what helps me get the interview where we get to know more about these people, I'm going to take it.”

Monica Barbaro at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Other panel highlights included the subject of ChatGPT, which only Guadagnino admitted to using occasionally to ask about what’s ok to feed his dogs. He also addressed parting ways with the film's original studio partner Amazon and the fortuitous partnership that emerged with new distributor NEON.

“I think there is some kind of honor in the decision because they could have written off the movie and that's it,” he said about Amazon dropping the film from their slate. “And then they allowed us to find a partner and we found the best partner possible… They really believed in the movie.”

“They really made everything to get us to make the best movie we could,” he continued. "I only have good feelings toward my friends at Amazon. And in a strange way, I kind of understand the decision. Conflict of interest is a big thing.”

Luca Guadagnino at Vanity Fair's Screening Room at LACMA on November 14, 2026

Of course, anyone who deletes their pre-load can install it again, though it might take some time given the game is 212GB.

The lucky winners will get a Steam key for Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, not a console code since the game's console plans haven't been confirmed yet, so that's something to keep in mind if you're taking part in this campaign.

If you were never planning to buy GTA 6 but still want to enter the contest, you can send a video of yourself biting into a raw onion to Devolver.

Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed, priced at $5 (or $3.74 until launch), releases on November 19, which is the same day that GTA 6 comes out. Reslimed was originally prototyped as a retro-style 2D platformer for Game Boy Color and was pitched by developer Doinksoft before the GTA 6 conversation really ramped up.

"There is no doubt GTA 6 will have the spotlight before, during, and after November 19, but it’s not for everyone, or releasing on Steam the same day, so we figure there’s a bit of counter-programming that may work in Volvy’s favor," Devolver told Kotaku.

GTA 6 has reportedly already sold nearly 15 million copies and generated about $1.5 billion in revenue.

#3550. Mom Begged Boyfriend to ‘Put the Gun Down’ Before He Killed Her, Her Daughter

A Florida man was arrested after he allegedly shot his girlfriend and her daughter to death and as one of his alleged victims begged him to “put the gun down.”

The Broward County Sheriff’s Office announced in a press release that David Keith Thornton has been charged with two counts of first-degree murder for his role in the deaths of his girlfriend, Suzanne Travers Courtade, and her daughter, Meghan Courtade.

Authorities were made aware of the incident on Thursday, November 12, when deputies received a report of a shooting around 7:21 p.m. at a Pompano Beach, Florida, home.

Suzanne, 66, called 911 and told dispatchers that her “daughter was shot by a pellet gun and is unconscious.” She then asked a neighbor for help before she screamed, “Dave put the gun down, put the gun down,” according to a probable cause arrest affidavit viewed by Law & Crime.

The dispatcher then heard a weapon fire multiple times. The same neighbor who was called for help later contacted 911 to report the alleged incident.

Once deputies responded, they discovered both Suzanne and Meghan, 23, dead in the street. Five spent .380-caliber shell casings were recovered near Thornton’s vehicle, while two additional 9 mm casings were located near another home.

Thornton, 64, had his hands up as he exited the home and said there were weapons inside, according to the affidavit.

The responding officers then entered the home, where they reportedly found weapons that matched the caliber of the recovered shell casings.

Investigators proceeded to speak to neighbors, with one person saying she thought the gunshots were loud fireworks. Soon after, Suzanne knocked on her door and explained that her daughter was unconscious and not breathing. The neighbor said she then went to Meghan and found her lying on the ground.

“While trying to assist Meghan, Thornton approached her and Suzanne and told [the neighbor], ‘This has nothing to do with you, go back inside,'” officers wrote in the affidavit.

The neighbor told officers that Thornton was holding a “dark object” in his hand, which she believed was a gun. She then ran to her home before she heard several gunshots.

Following his arrest, Thornton refused to speak with investigators. He is currently in custody at the Broward County Jail, where he is being held without bond.

Not much is known about Thornton’s dynamic with the victims, though police said that he, his girlfriend and her daughter had lived in the neighborhood for nearly two decades.

It’s not currently clear if Thornton has entered a plea or retained legal counsel following his arrest. The Broward County Sheriff’s Office did not immediately respond to Us’ request for comment regarding updates in the case.

#3549. Tallulah Willis: I Stayed Out Past My Bedtime to Celebrate My Mom at the Baby2Baby Gala

The whole endeavor began as it usually does, with a search for the perfect dress. Turns out it would be a yellow Carolina Herrera column-shaped confection (if you care), teetering on yellow satin pointed peekaboo-toe platforms, with my first press pass thudding around in my corresponding yellow duchess satin clutch.

Stylist Brad Goreski and his assistant Clarke, who work with my mother, Demi Moore, sourced the ensemble after finding Mom’s beautiful black ruffled two-piece (adorably also Carolina Herrera).

Around 6:50 p.m. on Saturday, my older sisters, Scout (in cocoa-brown beaded Elie Saab) and Rumer (in whimsical archival Vera Wang), florist Eric Buterbaugh, Brad, my mom and I are about to leave her house for the Baby2Baby Gala, an annual fundraiser for the non-profit that dedicated to providing diapers, clothing, and other basic necessities to children and families in need across the country.

Demi is taking photos against a pale brown backdrop when I hear her say, marginally worried, “Yes, the outfit is amazing, but they didn’t give me pockets.” I cannot fault her. A pocket, particularly in an evening gown, creates an entirely different architecture for one’s night.

When we make it to the Pacific Design Center in West Hollywood, Rihanna is blasting and a gorgeous electric General Motors car, part of the silent auction, is parked out front. I’m holding the bottom of my dress to avoid any “yard sales” on the carpeted floor when I hear, “Is it you? I hope it’s you!” It’s my very new, lovely friend Jackie Tohn, whom I met at a Nobody Wants This premiere party.

Inside, beautifully dressed people laugh and chat. I spot Miranda Kerr, who is both a Baby2Baby board member and major donor, and pass Nara Smith leaning over a dolled-up Elsa Hosk while “Espresso” blasts from overhead speakers.

Table 4 is front and center. Some could say the best seats in the house. Fitting, as Baby2Baby is honoring my mother with the Giving Tree Award tonight. The scene around our table is a frenzy of joyful energy. I make a beeline for Paris Hilton to thank her for the facial I received at her spa this week, while Dancing With the Stars alums Rumer and Jenna Dewan immediately pull out their phones to compare pictures of their kids.

Then I spot Sofia Richie Grainge and her husband, Atlantic Records CEO Elliot Grainge. I snake through throngs of elegant people and poke Elliot’s back twice. “Elliot, it’s Tallulah! We went to Wildwood together!” He instantly remembers me. “Tallulah was the cool girl in class,” he tells Sofia. I blush, but don’t feel the need to correct him.

Scout approaches and says, almost incredulously, “Hi, I’m Scout…you guys just signed me at Atlantic Records.” Elliot grabs her shoulders. “We’re so happy to have you. Are you happy with us?” She can’t say “yes” fast enough.

The program begins with Keke Palmer, who completely owns the stage, telling hilarious stories about her son before shifting into heartfelt candor about the gift of watching him grow. Kerry Washington thanks the sponsors and announces Baby2Baby’s new permanent headquarters, “a promise to millions of children. Not just for today, but for decades to come.”

Then Kelly Sawyer Patricof and Norah Weinstein, the organization’s CEOs, come to the stage, sharing the work—no, the magic—they have created over 15 years. Their first gala in 2012 raised $1 million. Last year’s raised $18 million. To date, they’ve distributed an astonishing 850 million essential items to people in need across all 50 states, responded to over 150 disasters, developed their own diaper production line during COVID, and expanded into mental health support for new mothers. The mission remains the same, but the scale is impossible to comprehend.

Now Rumer, Scout, and I are all crying during a short video about two families impacted by Baby2Baby. The feeling is palpable for the rest of the room.

As the live auction begins, I catch my mom discreetly reading over a printout of her speech. I don’t feel nerves coming off her, but a desire to match the elegance and integrity surrounding us.

Andrew Garfield takes the stage and speaks directly to my mom about the woman he knows. “She is a miracle,” he says.

Then it’s Demi’s turn. Holding her gleaming award in two hands, she thanks Andrew for carving out time amid his Artificial press tour. My mother adores Andrew, a feeling shared across our family.

Alone on stage in her Carolina gown (sans pockets), she asks everyone to breathe. “Inhale. Exhale.” That breath, she says, is the relief Baby2Baby provides when a mother no longer has to choose between dinner and diapers. “Your child matters, you matter, and you are not alone.” She leaves us with the idea that the essence of this work is to be remarkably human. Baby to baby, mother to mother, soul to soul.

Then Cardi B takes the stage and the atmosphere shifts with a jolt. Everyone is on their feet dancing. The official after-party begins, but I’m turning back into a pumpkin in towering satin stilettos. It was a remarkably beautiful night, and I’m left with the overwhelming desire to do more—to show up for someone who may not have the ability to show up for themselves or their precious loved ones.

But for this on-scene reporter’s inaugural correspondence, it was ultimately Baby2Baby2Bedtime.

#3548. There's a New Way to Automatically Back Up Your Android Photos for Free

In addition to Lifehacker, her work has been featured on Wirecutter, Tom’s Guide, and ZDNET. Emily has also worked as a travel guide around the U.S. and as a content editor. She has a masters in social work and is a licensed therapist in Utah.

If you're an Android user looking for a way to save your photos and videos without maxing out your cloud storage space, your device may soon be able to back up automatically to your PC. As spotted by Android Authority, Google included automatic backups from Android to Windows via Quick Share in its release notes for Google Play services v26.43.

Quick Share is a wireless file-sharing feature for Android that allows users to send photos, videos, and documents to nearby devices, including Windows computers and iPhones with AirDrop. The new automatic backup feature, which is likely to roll out gradually, uses Quick Share's functionality to transfer copies of photos and videos on your phone to your PC when nearby.

Since these backups happen locally, you don't need to rely solely on cloud storage in your Google account, nor do you need to remember to initiate transfers of photos and videos between devices. Plus, this is all free and doesn't require a separate cloud service subscription. While you can back up your media to Google Photos, as of earlier this year, more data from your Android backups count toward your Google Account storage cap unless you exclude specific types. Alternatively, you can also cobble together a decent amount of cloud storage from other providers at no extra cost, but automatic backups between Android and Windows minimize the likelihood that you'll forget to save data, and your PC provides plenty of space for free.

Once the feature is available on your device, you'll be able to initiate backups in the Quick Share for Windows app. Your Android and Windows devices must be in close proximity and signed into the same Google Account. You can toggle Automatic backups on and change the settings for what gets backed up and to where. The transfers will then occur wirelessly in the background.

As Android Authority reports, early hints at this feature suggested that Samsung phones and PCs would be excluded from automatic backups, but the release notes don't specify any further details.

The next big question on a lot of James Bond fans' minds, now that Robert Pattinson has been named the next Bond, is who will play the next “Bond Girl”? Though the rumors and anticipation haven’t quite reached the fevered pitch that the Bond casting rumors did, there is still plenty of speculation out there. My feeling on it is that it could be one of the frontrunners, like Sydney Sweeney or Margaret Qualley, but it’s just as likely to be a name we’ve not heard yet. With all that said, let’s get into some of the rumors.

Looking at the prediction markets like Kalshi, the leader right now to be the next Bond Girl is Margaret Qualley in the yet-untitled Bond 26. As of today, she’s sitting at about 60% odds to nab the role. This is after coming on strong in recent weeks, after Sydney Sweeney had been the favorite for months. Sweeney’s odds have dropped to about 10% recently, but I still think she should be considered a serious contender, given her trajectory over the last few years.

The only other actresses above 20% are Ana Taylor-Joy (25%) and Florence Pugh (20%). These rumors make a lot of sense, actually. Like Pattinson, they have both worked with Bond 26 director Denis Villeneuve in the Dune series. Until just recently, Pugh wasn’t among the speculation, really, but she’s a big part of the upcoming Dune: Part III, so perhaps Villeneuve may keep the band together.

That goes for Zendaya, too, who is currently sitting at 17% on Kalshi, but she seems less likely to me. Other names who appear on the list include Daisy Edgar-Jones, Jodie Comer, Emma Mackey, Alicia Vikander, and Vanessa Kirby. The final name on the current list is also an interesting one: Ana de Armas. She worked with Villeneuve on Blade Runner 2049, and she’s been in a James Bond movie before, playing a fellow spy in No Time to Die. That could make for an interesting dynamic.

So those are the top names on the prediction markets, but could it be someone else completely? Possible. These are pure speculation on my part, but how about Inde Navarrette? Her star is on the rise after her excellent performance in the surprise smash Obsession earlier in the 2026 movie schedule. She’s definitely someone to watch and could definitely draw some attention from the Bond producers, though she is scheduled to play Rogue in the 2028 X-Men movie, so she might not be available.

What about Jenna Ortega? She’s quickly becoming one of the biggest stars in the world (despite a recent stumble with Klara and the Sun) with her roles in Wednesday and the Scream franchise and could be a great fit for the role. Chloë Grace Moretz, someone else who has played Wednesday Addams, is another possibility. Someone like Sadie Sink would make a great Bond Girl, too. Though, like Navarrette, she may be tied up in the MCU franchise for the foreseeable future.

So what does the future hold? Let the speculation begin!

#3546. Windows Laptops Just Closed a Major Gap With the MacBook Neo

To say the MacBook Neo disrupted the laptop market would be an understatement. When the Neo dropped, former Apple CEO Tim Cook said Apple had its best-ever launch week for first-time Mac customers, and the company is reportedly planning on doubling the MacBook's sales for 2027. It's not hard to see why the MacBook Neo is such a hit: Apple is offering the essential Mac experience at a fantastic price point. You no longer need to spend $1,000 or more for a MacBook, so long as you're okay making some sacrifices to get there—which, it seems, many customers are.

While the MacBook Neo has been a boon for Apple and Apple fans alike, I can only imagine the stress it brought to PC manufacturers—especially those with budget or midrange machines. Windows PCs have long won the price war against Apple. While MacBooks have their passionate customers, buyers looking for the best value have had to weigh expensive Apple laptops against many far cheaper options from companies like Dell, HP, ASUS, and Lenovo. But with the Neo, suddenly a MacBook was competing in this space, and well.

Part of the issue for PC manufacturers was Apple's control over its own ecosystem. Unlike most PC makers, which only produce the hardware for each machine, Apple makes both the hardware and the software for its MacBook lineup. As such, the company has the advantage of optimizing that hardware. It can design macOS to run more efficiently on weaker hardware, in a way that companies like Dell or ASUS can't. You might be comparing the MacBook Neo against a Windows laptop with similar specs, or even better specs, but because Microsoft makes Windows, not the laptop manufacturer, it's possible the Neo ends up with the better overall experience. While that might still be the case, Microsoft may have just closed that gap in a meaningful way.

This week, Microsoft announced key upgrades to memory-management efficiency, particularly for machines with 8GB of RAM. This is the amount of memory the MacBook Neo has, as well as many budget and midrange Windows laptops. That's not much memory for 2026, regardless of platform, but Apple seems to have squeezed a lot out of it for the Neo. Now, Microsoft may have just done the same for PCs, as Windows is reportedly 20% more responsive, with 40% faster multitasking.

In its blog post, Microsoft highlighted improvements that users with 8 GB of RAM can expect from Windows going forward. First, Microsoft says it focused on better utilizing the RAM your machine already has. The company compares its memory management to a desk: Anything on the "desk" is stored in RAM; anything in your "drawer" is stored in your drive. As you use your PC, Windows used to move more of your apps and tabs to your drawer to free up more RAM for other things, meaning you'd need to reload those items whenever you returned to them. Going forward, the company says that Windows can keep up to 2GB more of your active data in RAM instead of moving it to slower storage elsewhere. That means apps and tabs should refresh less frequently when you leave and return to them.

Microsoft also says that small actions should be faster across the board. When you open the Start menu, search across your PC, right-click, open Settings, launch the Snipping Tool, and open File Explorer, those actions may be up to 20% faster than they were in January. Microsoft Edge may open up to 33% faster, while Teams can enable Efficiency Mode by default on 8 GB machines, which means it can launch up to 20% faster too. Microsoft put together an interesting stress test to compare multitasking performance between today and January. It opened 20 tabs in Edge, a 4K video, large Word, PowerPoint, and Excel files, then Outlook and File Explorer, all without closing any windows. That experience was 40% faster following this latest update.

Microsoft says it also improved the memory efficiency in its apps: The company claims it reduced committed-memory growth by up to 900 MB, and saved up to 360 MB in RAM across Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and Outlook. That extends to third-party apps as well: Microsoft says that WhatsApp has double-digit memory improvement now. Widgets also only load when you open the app, which saves 200 MB of RAM when the app is closed, while Edge tabs go inactive after 15 minutes instead of two hours.

Microsoft isn't making these upgrades in a vacuum. Hardware costs, particularly for RAM, have skyrocketed in the age of AI. Microsoft knows that people are likely going to hold onto existing hardware for longer than they usually do, or that they'll opt for less-expensive configurations, including, perhaps, machines with 8 GB of RAM.

PCMag's Chris Hoffman was adamant before this latest Windows update that buyers should steer clear of PCs with 8 GB of RAM. Now, he's pulling back a bit. In his testing, Hoffman noticed improvements when multitasking on an 8 GB PC when compared to similar tests from months ago. He could run multiple Chrome tabs, a Microsoft Word window, and Spotify without bogging down the computer much. Hoffman isn't a lightweight user, so he still wouldn't personally choose an 8 GB machine, but he admits, "If I were an average PC buyer looking for a reasonable desktop experience and could save hundreds of dollars by opting for 8GB of RAM, I might be happy with the performance."

To that point, I think this new Windows update makes 8 GB PCs competitive, especially against the MacBook Neo. We'll still need direct comparisons to know how well this new Windows experience holds up across the board, but these updates are promising. Users with 8 GB machines just got a free, valuable update overnight; new customers can opt for a more affordable PC without feeling like performance will take a nosedive just because they opened one too many Edge tabs.

As Hoffman says, 8 GB of RAM is not ideal for any user looking for serious multitasking or professional workflows, regardless of whether they choose a Mac or PC. But for the average computer customer looking for a solid machine without breaking the bank, I no longer see the Neo as necessarily the default choice. After all, Apple has slowly raised its price, too, from $599 to $699. If you're platform-agnostic, or even prefer Windows to macOS, these updates from Microsoft are quite promising. If you're in the market, check out PCMag's excellent list of budget laptop recommendations.
