Danny Kilby showed on Survivor that he had guts after threatening to go to rocks to keep ally Lewis Kelly safe. That was bold, but I never would've imagined he'd be so bold as to execute that exact strategy in a bid to win back all his belongings after Season 51. Unfortunately, his attempt to recreate Storage Wars ended in disaster, but it makes for a hilarious story.

Kilby posted on TikTok about how he moved out of his apartment before Survivor and put all his furniture possessions in a storage locker. Unfortunately, just before leaving, he got a new debit card and realized he forgot to change his billing information with the facility. He said:

So I call them, I spam them, I send emails. There’s no way to get a hold of them on the weekend, and they’re like, oh, you can transfer that details on Monday. Well, I’m like, I’m flying to Fiji before then, so I kind of just rolled the dice and hoped it worked out.

It feels like there were more options on the table than "see what happens," especially since he was staying with his girlfriend, who might've been able to call on his behalf. I guess I shouldn't be surprised that the same guy who gave a guy a case of beer to teach him to swim would have this kind of casual attitude about all of his things.

Kilby goes on Survivor, has a memorable run, gains a love of aquadumping, but ultimately gets voted out next to Kristin Flickinger. Of course, as a part of the jury, he didn't return home until Season 51 was over. Kilby picked up things from there:

I get back to Canada, the first email I read was, hey, we were not able to reach you, so your stuff is going up for auction unless you pay like $2000 in storage fees or whatever. And I went, I can’t afford 2000 bucks right now, so that sucks. But then I was like, wait, what if I bid at an auction on my own stuff? I made my own Storage Wars, you know what I mean?

He had just gotten off of one of the best reality shows, and he wanted to recreate the experience from another show. Granted, the stakes were much higher on Storage Wars, as Kilby planned on trying to outbid competitors on all of his belongings to get a discount.

Unfortunately, he didn't win that Survivor money, and as such, didn't have a ton to spare for the auction. Readers can guess where things are headed, but it's great to hear him recap how it all went down:

It goes up to 400 bucks. And that’s about as much as I had…Part of me had this whole like after Survivor, I’m just like a minimalist now, man. I don’t need stuff. I lost the bid to my own stuff, so somebody named Prince C now owns all of my belongings, my couch, my cheetah painting where he’s dressed as a general. I called him 'General Cheetah.'

The wildest part of this story is that Kilby only had $400 dollars, and according to a photo he shared on TikTok, the winning bid was $442. Couldn't he have found a friend or family member to float him an extra hundred? I can't imagine losing everything in my apartment over less than $50.

Learning this makes me think Kilby had a worse exit from Survivor than both Rhode Island Rob and Brady. How can you go on a reality show to win money and leave with a lot less than you started with? Maybe this story will convince Jeff Probst to bring him back sooner rather than later, so he can get a new couch or a portrait of a cheetah dressed as a general.

Kilby is like the poster boy for Survivor's changes to casting in Season 51, and I'm here for it. Finding people who were capable of risking it all to win was a good call, and it's resulted in some real chaos. So chaotic, in fact, people were discussing eating corn from poop, but fortunately even the wilder players shied away from that.

Catch new episodes of Survivor on CBS on Wednesdays at 8:00 p.m. ET. With these latest eliminations, I'm not sure who will end up winning it all. I will say I have no shortage of favorites, however, and wouldn't mind seeing a few people take home the grand prize.

Curry Barker's Obsession is one of the year's best horror films, but his next movie might end up being even better. Barker is writing, directing, and starring in next year's Anything but Ghosts, and he'll be joined by a horror movie icon.

Anything but Ghosts stars Barker, his longtime collaborator Cooper Tomlinson (who's also co-writing it), Bryce Dallas Howard, and Aaron Paul. Lillard broke through with his role as Stu Macher in the original Scream and reprised the role in Scream 7, released earlier this year. He's also starred in Five Nights at Freddy's, its sequel, and the latest adaptation of Carrie.

Aside from Scream, Lillard might be best known for his role as Shaggy in the early 2000s Scooby-Doo movies. He then went on to voice the character in several animated films and TV specials over the years.

#3530. James Bond Fans React To Robert Pattinson's 007 Casting

Robert Pattinson has spent his career ping-ponging between major franchise fare ("Harry Potter," "Twilight," "The Batman") and weird arthouse fare ("The Lighthouse," "Good Time," "Cosmopolis"). Along the way, he's garnered a pretty broad fanbase, so there are plenty of people celebrating the news that Pattinson will be taking over the role of James Bond.

There were several other finalists to play the next Bond, including Josh O'Connor, Jack Lowden, and Nicholas Hoult, but Pattinson was the clear frontrunner even before he was announced. Early reactions to the news have noted the somewhat absurd flex of landing the role of James Bond just a few years after landing the role of Batman. "This is the greed they talk about in the Bible," wrote one user on Reddit.

Casting such a well-known actor in the role of Bond bucks the trend of 007 casting, with previous revamps traditionally favoring actors who weren't already firmly established. Many people, while not necessarily disliking the choice of Pattinson for the role, have pointed out that Amazon isn't exactly taking a risk. Other Reddit users describe Pattinson as "a very conservative choice" and "very safe casting," with one wryly commenting, "This isn't beating the allegations of 'every movie has the same five actors in it.'" So, while casting a lesser-known actor would surely have attracted some controversy in its own right, some Bond fans feel that the safety of this choice is "disappointing."

And, of course, there are Batman fans who fear that this fresh commitment spells the end of Pattinson's tenure as the Dark Knight. Between production delays on "The Batman II," a recent power shake-up at DC Studios, and now this 007 casting news, the general assumption is that Pattinson's Batman will be hanging up his cape after two movies.

One of the upsides of having such an eccentric career and personality is that Robert Pattinson has generated a great many memes over the years — and now they're being put to good use. One Tumblr user adapted a famous "Twilight" scene to have Pattinson's Edward Cullen saying, "This is the skin of a [license to kill]er," Bella." Others, meanwhile, have joked that we "finally have a Gen Z James Bond," in reference to a Vanity Fair interview wherein Pattinson doggedly insists that he is Gen Z and that the year he was born "doesn't matter."

One meme that became popular even before Pattinson was officially cast imagines the reactions of the other hopefuls auditioning for the role when they see the unstoppable Pattinson walk in after them.

every other actor when robert pattinson shows up to audition pic.twitter.com/40fHsnS2C4

— ivy (@ohhhhhherewegoo) November 16, 2026

Fans are particularly amused by the fact that Pattinson showed up "late" to the audition process (which has been going on for years), sandwiching it in between his commitments to "Dune: Part Three" and "The Batman Part II," and still landed the role. But that kind of effortless swagger only makes him more perfect for the role of James Bond.

#3529. Billy Crystal Answers the Proust Questionnaire

Which historical figure do you most identify with?

My wife, Janice. Fearless, smart, optimistic, hilarious, loving…adored by all.

What is the trait you most deplore in yourself?

Self-doubt. Wait, now I’m not sure of the answer. Was that okay? Can we come back to that one?

What is the trait you most deplore in others?

From my dressing room to backstage—standing alone in the dark, a deep breath, and then feeling it’s time and walking out into the light.

It’s no secrets that celebrities can be major superfans, even getting starstruck or seeking out advice from their acting heroes. Though this may be the first time I’ve heard of an actor trolling a celebrity who isn’t the Rock poking fun at friend Kevin Hart. I didn’t expect Off Campus’ Stephen Kalyn to admit he trolled Timothèe Chalamet HARD at the beginning of his career.

The actor’s career has since taken off thanks to his starring role as Dean Di Laurentis in the hockey romance series. Before that he had a recurring role in shows like Gen V and Motorheads, and apparently, he admired Chalamet’s career and reached out to the Dune actor for tips. It reached the point that his "trolling" became a bit. The Elite Daily shares what the actor had to say about his DMing days:

This is, like, kind of embarrassing. I went on Instagram and I DM’d him, and I was like, ‘Hey, man! Just letting you know, I’m new in the business, and if you have any tips or whatever, let a guy know. I really loved your work in Call Me By Your Name, Beautiful Boy.’ He never responded to me.

The actor clearly has no problems being totally open even if it could be embarrassing. Honestly, I respect it. While his former pastime is a little "unhinged," I doubt Chalamet even noticed given he probably gets MANY messages from fans. Though I don’t blame Kalyn for admiring the actor’s confidence or how fast his career seemed to take off. His admiration is clearly being channeled into his many shirtless scenes on Off Campus, which he has shared can be a little “uncomfortable” at times though leaves him feeling ready to conquer the world. Definitely Chalamet-level energy.

However, his admission had a mix of reactions from fans in the comments. Some understand Kalyn’s admiration, such as kandiboober who shares, “I text him a lot too. Usually, I send him pie recipes and grocery lists.” Others feel like it’s the equivalent of texting a celebrity happy birthday when you know you won’t get a response. Though for a while a lack of response didn’t stop Kalyn from checking in “every month,” as he continues:

It just became a bit at that point. I was like ‘hey, man, you up?’ or ‘hey, what’s up? You gonna respond to that DM?’

The actor doesn’t say how long the "trolling" lasted. However, a few fans feel like he could have kept that information to himself. Although this isn’t the strangest thing a celebrity has done or even the most dedicated. We can’t forget Emma Stone’s wild story about trying to catching a glimpse of a Real Housewife. As far as I know Kalyn has yet to cross paths with Chalamet in person. Though given his career is on the rise there could be a time when they’ll be on the same red carpet and he’ll have a chance to speak to him.

In the meantime, Kalyn is busy filming Season 2 of Off Campus and even doing commercials for Verizon, which is set to premiere in April 2027. So for now, it seems his pastime ‘trolling’ has fallen to the side.

You can catch up on Season 1 and see every shirtless moment with an Amazon Prime subscription. However, Chalamet doesn't make an appearance in the popular series.

#3527. ChatGPT's New GIF Generator Is Fun, but Won't Replace Us Humans (Yet)

Khamosh Pathak is a freelance tech journalist with over 13 years of experience writing online. An accounting graduate, he turned his interest in writing and technology into a career. He holds a specialization in user experience design from ISDI Parsons in Mumbai, where he sought to deepen his understanding of UX, consumer devices, and interplay between software and technology.

Khamosh has written thousands of how-tos and guides on every major platform (iOS, macOS, Android, and Windows). He got started writing how-tos and guides for Guiding Tech, where he also published several e-books. His work has also been seen at MakeUseOf, How-To Geek, and PCMag. He is truly passionate about brewing good coffee.

When it comes to generating AI images, both Gemini and ChatGPT do a passable job. In most cases, the results will look AI-generated, but they likely won’t have glaring spelling issues or missing limbs. Now, OpenAI is trying something new, introducing GIF support for ChatGPT. It's the company's first "moving images" feature since OpenAI shut down Sora, and while you can generate hyper-realistic videos in Gemini, this new ChatGPT feature is trying to fill in the gap, in a small way.

OpenAI is pitching the new feature as an animation tool, not exactly as a way to create looping videos—though that’s how I ended up using it. You give ChatGPT a prompt, as detailed as you can make it, and the chatbot produces a GIF in just a few seconds. You can start with your own drawings or images, too. ChatGPT uses sketches as the base for animations, though it can turn any still image into animated GIFs. Like other AI editing tools, you can edit it if ChatGPT didn't quite get it right: You can ask ChatGPT to make the GIF longer or shorter, remove certain objects, change the style, slow down transitions, among other edits.

AI art can be quite sterile, but I was surprised by how adding motion and animation to the mix makes generating images a lot more fun. Unlike traditional GIFs, which usually pull from existing video clips, you can turn anything you want into a GIF, which is especially cool if you're using your own art. In my testing, I found this to be the most rewarding part. It’s not always possible to one-shot a GIF with a single prompt. But after a few rounds of edits, I ended up creating some GIFs that I actually wanted to share in my WhatsApp groups.

That being said, I think human-made GIFs are still the gold standard here. For example, I asked ChatGPT to generate a video of someone brewing a pour-over, with a gooseneck kettle, showing the coffee blooming process. It did okay, but it’s nothing like actually making a pour-over. The kettle doesn’t move in circles, the water doesn’t rise evenly, there are no bubbles, and the steam is all over the place.

Compare that to the GIF below, which comes from a royalty-free video. Even though it’s a compressed, low-quality, and noisy GIF, it still shows the movement of the pour, the water rising, and even the bubbles. The details captured by a real video just aren’t there in ChatGPT GIFs. If that’s what you’re expecting, you will be disappointed. But I don't think that's the point of this feature anyway.

I found that ChatGPT excels when you’re making something fun, and you don’t look into the details too much. It pulled off a loop of a cat playing with a ball, and it was great at making a festive GIF for Diwali. It even made a GIF based on a photo. I asked it to create a fun promotional GIF for my JBL Bluetooth speakers, and it did the job quite well. At first, the transitions were too jarring, and the movement just made no sense. After some editing, though, I got it to a decent place.

Still, the main issue with ChatGPT GIFs is that complex movement and transitions aren’t nailed down. A hand shifts position weirdly between frames, and colors and objects appear out of nowhere. But if you can get over these issues, you can make some fun, lighthearted GIFs and memes to share with your friends on Instagram or WhatsApp.

#3526. Robert Pattinson's James Bond Casting Breaks A 60-Year-Old 007 Tradition

It's official: We have our new 007. Robert Pattinson has been cast as the next James Bond and will take over for Daniel Craig, whose run concluded in 2021 with "No Time to Die." Now, a full five years later, Amazon and MGM have finally firmed up who will be filling in the legendary character's shoes for his latest cinematic chapter. And while Pattinson is undoubtedly an actor with a lot of experience, his casting does break a tradition that has been going for more than 60 years.

1962's "Dr. No" kicked off cinema's most enduring franchise with "James Bond," based on Ian Fleming's series of novels. Sean Connery famously played 007 in that movie, with his run expanding through 1971's "Diamonds are Forever." He did return to the part once more for "Never Say Never Again," but that's not technically an official entry in the "Bond" movie canon. In any case, it's the role that went on to define Connery's career, as it generally has for every other actor who's picked up the baton after him.

Becoming James Bond was a double-edged sword for Connery, as it was at times hard for people to see him as anything other than the famed MI6 spy. But that was sort of by design. What the producers of the "Bond" franchise generally did was cast an actor who had experience but wasn't necessarily an A-list movie star. That allowed them to truly become Bond, not just on screen but in the eyes of the viewing public. That's where Pattinson truly differs.

Pattinson broke out as Edward Cullen in the "Twilight" films before starring in a string of acclaimed indies. More recently, he played Bruce Wayne in "The Batman." That matters a lot.

Robert Pattinson isn't just a big movie star, he's one who has a handful of beloved characters under his belt. A lot of people will always associate him with "Twilight." That's why it was hard for certain folks to see him as Batman until "The Batman" came out. People are now going to see him as the Caped Crusader for years to come, especially with "The Batman Part II" in the works.

Amazon currently controls the "James Bond" films, though, and it's willing to buck tradition. Amazon's Jeff Bezos reached his breaking point with the franchise's original producers, Barbara Broccoli and Michael G. Wilson, ultimately buying them out. Had Broccoli and Wilson been involved, it's less likely that an actor with as much cache as Pattinson would have won out against the likes of Callum Turner ("Eternity") and Josh O'Connor ("Challengers"), who were among the finalists.

On paper, Pattinson does fit the bill in every other way. James Bond is never young, and Pattinson is 40. That's almost the exact same age that Pierce Brosnan was when he took over for "GoldenEye." Roger Moore was 45 when he took over in "Live and Let Die." Even Daniel Craig was 38 in "Casino Royale," which was an origin story for him as 007. He's meant to be a seasoned veteran. He's not a rookie. But Moore ("The Saint") and Brosnan ("Remington Steele") were more TV stars than movie stars.

There's no denying that Pattinson has the look. We've seen him shine in suits in movies like "Tenet" and "Cosmopolis." He's also turned into one heck of an actor and is currently in the mix to win Best Actor at next year's Oscars for his role in "Primetime."

It also doesn't hurt that the actor previously worked with director Denis Villeneuve on "Dune: Part Three," which hits theaters in December. After that, Villeneuve is heading right into production on the currently untitled "James Bond 26." There's a rapport there between the two. It's easy to see the appeal of Robert Pattinson as 007, particularly for Amazon.

Much has changed in Hollywood in the 20 years since Daniel Craig took over for Pierce Brosnan in "Casino Royale." James Bond isn't the slam dunk movie star he once was, so to speak, and Amazon needs this franchise to work for a new generation. Casting a bankable star like Pattinson, whom audiences very much like, adds some insurance. Case in point, Christopher Nolan's "The Odyssey" (which co-stars Pattinson) has ruled the box office with more than $1.8 billion to its name this year. So, Pattinson has a great track record even outside of big franchises.

Naturally, fans are going to feel big feelings about Pattinson as Bond. Craig has no hard feelings about his "Casino Royale" casting controversy, but it's worth remembering that people flipped out when he was announced. Now? He's perhaps the most beloved actor in the franchise's history. The actor has to prove himself once he's cast, regardless of what fans think. That's always been the case.

Pattinson absolutely has to shoulder that same responsibility now. The question is, can people see him as James Bond more than Edward Cullen or Batman? Can he assert himself as Bond so definitively that his history doesn't overshadow what's on screen? That's some extra baggage that his predecessors didn't necessarily have to carry.

The new "James Bond" movie doesn't have a release date yet, but stay tuned.

#3525. Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond

It looks like Robert Pattinson is trading in his Batmobile for an Aston Martin. After a highly scrutinized and lengthy audition process involving some of Hollywood’s most sought-after leading men, it was the Batman star who emerged at the eleventh hour to nab the role of MI6 agent James Bond.

“James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honor of a lifetime,” said Pattinson in a statement. “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya, and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me. To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement. I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”

Created by Ian Fleming for his 1953 novel Casino Royale, James Bond, the British intelligence officer who lends his immense talents to MI6, is one of the most recognizable characters in the modern world. Figuring prominently in 12 of Fleming’s novels and two collections of short stories, Bond is both tall, dark, and handsome and calm, cool, and collected—the platonic ideal of a world-class spy. Bond leapt from page to screen in 1962 with the Eon-produced Dr. No, spawning one of the biggest media franchises in history. Since its inception, the 27 Bond films have grossed more than $7 billion dollars worldwide.

Pattinson follows in the suave footsteps of Daniel Craig, who played James Bond for five films, from 2006’s Casino Royale until 2021’s No Time to Die where (spoiler alert) Craig’s 007 dies while protecting the world from a global terrorist organization. Around No Time to Die, there was another shake up in Bond ownership when Amazon acquired Bond’s parent studio, MGM, in an $8.5 billion deal. Barbara Broccoli—whose father, Eon founder Albert R. “Cubby” Broccoli, produced the first Bond film—and her half brother, Michael G. Wilson, held the rights to the franchise for almost 30 years, and pledged to work with Amazon. However, in February 2025, Broccoli and Wilson announced that they’d be stepping back from the franchise and ceding complete creative control to Amazon MGM. At the Oscars a month later, the Broccoli family was honored with a bizarre musical tribute to James Bond, starring Margaret Qualley, Doja Cat, and Lisa, unofficially ushering in a new era in the Bond Cinematic Universe.

Although a new era of Bond loomed, Amazon MGM had one major problem: They needed a new Bond. Ahead of No Time to Die, Craig had announced that he was stepping away from the franchise, leaving the producers with a 007-sized hole to fill. Before she stepped away, Broccoli insinuated that this new era of Bond was looking for a younger actor, in their 30s, to take over the reins from Craig, who was 51 when he retired from MI6.

Technically, they landed on someone slightly outside their preferred age range; Pattinson is 40 years old. Just don’t tell him that. During Vanity Fair’s lie detector test with Jennifer Lawrence while promoting their film Die My Love, Pattinson insisted he was from a different generation. I am Gen Z,” he said to Lawrence. “I am.” Hey, you’re only as old as you feel. In the same video, Pattinson said he “likes taking jobs of younger actors,” which he managed to do with his Bond casting. Good for Pattinson.

Almost every leading man in Hollywood’s name came up as a potential predecessor to Craig—except for Pattinson, who the masses assumed was out of contention due to the fact that he locked into playing another beloved fictional character with massive IP: Batman. Pattinson’s take on the caped crusader in Matt Reeve’s The Batman (2022) was a major success, but several production delays on The Batman Part II, and a shakeup at Batman’s studio, DC—last week, it was announced that the co-CEOs of DC Productions, James Gunn and Peter Safran, were ousted from the studio—meant that there might be time in Pattinson’s schedule for some sexy espionage.

Still, it was far from a done deal that Pattinson would land 007. In recent years, some fans have advocated for a twist on the classic Bond formula. Lashana Lynch made history as Nomi, the first Black person to ever to hold the 007 moniker, in No Time to Die. But Nomi is not James Bond. There was a seemingly endless period when the world was convinced that Idris Elba—arguably the most tall, dark, and handsome man to ever exist—would take on the mantle at some point, but it wasn’t meant to be. Now, at 53, Elba has seemingly aged out of the role. (For the record, Elba thought the next Bond should be a woman.) Elba wasn’t the only name bandied about in recent years. It was reported in 2024 that Aaron Taylor-Johnson was close to signing a contract to take over the role, but those reports were never confirmed.

Although a favorite at the beginning, Jacob Elordi reportedly didn’t screen test for the role. Riz Ahmed made an Emmy-nominated television show, Bait, inspired by the idea of a British Pakistani actor getting cast as Bond. Other actors rumored to be in the mix over the course of the process include, but are not limited to, Tom Francis, Harris Dickinson, and, apparently, Harry Styles. At the end of the day, five actors reportedly screen-tested for the role: Slow Horse’s Jack Lowden, One Night Only’s Callum Turner, Disclosure Day’s Josh O’Connor, Superman’s Nicholas Hoult, and Pattison. Hoult and Pattinson were the last names to emerge as contenders for the role, implying that the powers that be at Amazon MGM may not have been happy with the three options presented and sent a hail mary. When Puck reported that Pattinson was able to negotiate a three-picture deal rather than a four-picture deal despite commanding a much higher salary than the other options, it looked like the writing was on the wall that Pattinson would be the next Bond.

It also helps that Pattinson is having a career high at the moment, having starred in a handful of the most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films of 2026. He began the year by turning his controversial A24 comedy The Drama with Zendaya into a box-office success, generating $134 million worldwide on a reported budget of about $28 million. He then followed that up with a deliciously sniveling turn in Christopher Nolan’s epic The Odyssey, an Oscar front-runner that earned $1.8 billion at the box office. Then there’s Primetime, the Lance Oppenheim drama starring Pattinson as To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen. (Yes, in a way, Chris Hansen is now one degree from being James Bond. Let that sink in). Primetime hit big with $62 million globally on an $14.5 million budget, and is earning Pattinson leading-actor buzz. On top of it all, he’s still got Dune: Part Three with Denis Villeneuve coming down the pipeline in December.

Ultimately, the Twilight star was handpicked by the powers that be at Amazon MGM, including producers Amy Pascal and David Heyman and director Denis Villeneuve, who is helming the next iteration of the series based on a script from screenwriter Steven Knight, with Tanya Lapointe executive producing. Given the fact that Pattinson is starring in Villeneuve’s highly-anticipated Dune: Part Three, it might not be that much of a surprise that the director chose Pattinson as his next Bond. “Before anything else, I want to express my deep gratitude to the remarkable actors who joined us on this journey,” said Villeneuve in a statement. “We were surrounded by extraordinary talent, but there can only be one 007. I am overjoyed to welcome Robert Pattinson as our new James Bond. He has the timeless soul of 007 and brings a spirit that is completely new. I cannot wait to begin.”

Pattinson enters a long lineage of spectacularly suave spies—some who lasted longer than others in Bond’s impeccably tailored suits. The first-ever James Bond was, of course, Sean Connery, who went on to star in six Bond films, including From Russia With Love (1963), Goldfinger (1964), and Diamonds Are Forever (1971). Connery was followed by George Lazenby, who starred in a single Bond film, On Her Majesty’s Secret Service (1969), before passing the reins back to Connery. The third Bond was Roger Moore, who took over for 1973’s Live and Let Die, and appeared in a total of seven Bond films, most notably The Spy Who Loved Me (1977) and Octopussy (1983).

After Moore came Timothy Dalton, who became 007 with 1987’s The Living Daylights, then threw in the towel after 1989’s License to Kill. Millennials will fondly remember the next Bond: Pierce Brosnan, who starred as the sexy spy in four films from 1995’s GoldenEye to 2002’s Die Another Day, until Craig took over in 2006.

Will Pattison’s Bond be more debonair like Brosnan, who told VF he was “eagerly” awaiting the Bond casting news, or brooding like Craig? Will he be remembered as a rightful heir to Connery’s throne, or will his Bond feel closer to Austin Powers in The Spy Who Shagged Me? In any case, let’s hope Pattinson prefers his martinis shaken not stirred. He’s going to be drinking a lot of them for the foreseeable future.

#3524. 10 Shows Like 'Cyberpunk: Edgerunners' You Should Watch Next

Ross Johnson writes about television, film, and literature for Lifehacker. He has a degree in political science from the University of Rochester and has previously been a legal writer and editor for Thomson Reuters, for which he later traveled around India and the Middle East as an educator specializing in American English style and grammar for adults.

Ross has been an actor on stage, in commercials, and in independent films since childhood, and has written hundreds of articles and essays on genre literature and cinema for Barnes & Noble, Gizmodo, Kotaku, and Yahoo! Entertainment.Ross produces the Swan Songs film podcast and hosts The Sound of Tomorrow, a pop culture and current affairs radio show based in Rochester, New York, where he lives with his husband and dogs and supports the local arts and cinema scene. You can find him on Bluesky.

This is Streamalikes, where you can find a curated list of recommendations to stream based on what you already like.

Following the dramatic conclusion of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners way back in 2022, the show has returned for a new season set in the megalopolis of Night City with a standalone story and a new cast of characters (by necessity).

Though the aesthetic and themes of cyberpunk have their roots in American science fiction of the 1970s and '80s, anime and manga of the '90s and beyond embraced the form and took it to entirely new places—so much so that a Japanese/Polish co-production of an adaptation of a video game from a Polish designer has taken its cues from a couple of decades' worth of great anime and cerebral sci-fi. Which is to say, if you're looking for more heady sci-fi series, these 10 are a good place to start.

An iconic, effortlessly cool genre classic, Cowboy Bebop is one of the undisputed GOATs of anime, blending western, noir, and crime genres and setting the resultant mash to a killer soundtrack of old-school jazz (which serves much the same purpose as Cyberpunk's propulsive electronic grooves). The title's "cowboys" are bounty hunters in a near-future in which humans have been forced to colonize the solar system after Earth became uninhabitable. Different settings, but both shows offer up ragtag crews with highly dubious fates. Former hitman Spike Spiegel leads his crew on one nearly disastrous mission after another, their standalone adventures all building to a thoroughly memorable climax. Stream Cowboy Bebop on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

This one's set in 22nd-century Japan, with a slick Blade Runner-esque aesthetic and a setup reminiscent of Minority Report. Here, technology exists to measure intentions, so crimes can be stopped before they’ve occurred, at which point the “criminals” are placed into psychological treatment (à la A Clockwork Orange)—or subject to summary execution because their threat potential is too high. That ability to predict behavior bleeds over into every aspect of life: careers and even relationships are determined in large part by the same systems that sniff out criminal intent. Obviously, this is all perfectly fine, and there’s no potential for abuse or miscalculation whatsoever...though there are a couple of warning signs. The first involves a new Enforcer who becomes a potential murderer himself when he miscalculates the extent of a criminal’s potential to do wrong, and, even more significantly, the existence of a criminal mastermind who is somehow invisible to the tech, even as his criminal actions grow more and more elaborate. Stream Psycho-Pass on Prime Video and Crunchyroll.

Created by Tim Miller and with director David Fincher as an executive producer, this animated anthology series is a grab bag of wildly diverse offerings: Each episode is produced by a different international studio, with the only link between them being one of the three words in the show's title. One episode deals with robotic gladiator fights in dystopian London, another finds us under the threat of sentient yogurt, yet another finds an ambitious cat learning to make use of a family's robot helper. Its format dictates that no two episodes are going to have the same premise, but it shares with Cyberpunk an edgy sensibility and stories set in an apocalyptic future, albeit with a dark sense of humor—its four seasons offer up a mix of tech, sex, violence, and gorgeous animation. Stream Love, Death & Robots on Netflix.

One of several completely standalone spinoffs of the wildly influential 1995 film (itself based on the beloved manga series), Stand Alone Complex requires no prior knowledge. The style is largely the draw, as the series luxuriates in its fictional Nihama City setting, a world unto itself in a future Japan in which cybernetic people hack directly into the internet. Our sympathies are more with the authorities—in this case, Public Security Section 9, a cybercrime and antiterrorism police unit—than the cyber criminals, but the show approaches some of the same themes as Edgerunners with legit punk style. Stream Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex on Tubi and The Criterion Channel.

In this adaptation of the Richard K. Morgan cyberpunk classic of the same name, Joel Kinnaman and Anthony Mackie (yes, both of them) star as Takeshi "Tak" Kovacs. In this future megacity setting, human consciousness can be transferred between bodies. The tech is widely available, but only the wealthy can afford the backups and protections that make it a form of virtual immortality. Kovacs is a former soldier turned mercenary, revived from a backup after 200 years by Laurens Bancroft (James Purefoy), one of the wealthiest men alive. His motives for bringing the man back are shrouded in mystery, but he's giving Tak a chance to solve a very cold case: his own murder. Stream Altered Carbon on Netflix.

Another popular (and Emmy-winning) game adaptation, Arcane is based on League of Legends, a top-down actioner involving online opponents shooting lasers across a map. It doesn't sound like fodder for a show this impressive, but here we are. The League of Legends lore forms the backdrop for the show, but the pull is in the narrative involving two sisters caught up in the growing conflict between a utopian city and its oppressed underclass, without whom it couldn’t exist. The painted animation style is truly something special—not a stylistic match for Cyberpunk, but the two shows both go far above and beyond to create striking visual worlds. Stream Arcane on Netflix.

Vash the Stampede is a hunted outcast with a dark history that slowly comes to light over the course of the series. He’s got a reputation as a human wrecking ball, bringing destruction wherever he goes, and seemingly just for fun—but in reality he’s far more respectful of life than his pursuers. Still, cities evacuate at the mere possibility of his arrival, and a huge bounty sits on his head (no matter that the bounty hunters do far more damage than Vash). He and his friends—actually a couple of insurance agents—find themselves in a series of misadventures on the planet Gunsmoke, building to a final showdown that caps the series with finality. Visually, it’s probably one of the defining ‘90s shōnen-style action series, with elegantly choreographed gunfights that never get old. Tonally similar, Trigun also shares with Cyberpunk 2 the work of legendary composer Tsuneo Imahori, his music being crucial to both shows. Stream Trigun on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

Another from animation studio Trigger, Darling in the Franxx leans heavily into the mecha sub-genre, set in a post-apocalypse where children are bred and indoctrinated into piloting the title's massive Franxx to defend the remnants of humanity. Adults are pretty much immortal, so the kids simply don't have any other utility. Two of these teens begin to develop romantic feelings for each other, potentially complicating their usefulness to society and leading to an explosive, bittersweet finale. Stream Darling in the Franxx on Crunchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

What starts out as a relatively straightforward action show about space bounty hunters (the title's “Killjoys”) develops surprising depth over the course of its five seasons. As officially sanctioned Killjoys, the trio at the show’s heart (Hannah John-Kamen, Aaron Ashmore, and Luke Macfarlane) are bound to remain politically neutral at any cost. Initially, that’s a way to get them right into the heat of a fight, but as they develop ties of friendship and family in an exploited community, they come to understand the high cost of unchecked wealth and greed, and the ways in which neutrality always benefits the oppressors. The show’s creators make exceptionally good use of a limited budget and offer up some impressive queer rep along the way, a rarity in pop sci-fi. Stream Killjoys on Tubi or buy it from Prime Video and Apple TV.

Another great cyberpunk metropolis: here it's Kansai, an increasingly lawless city run by elite criminals known as Akudama. An ordinary girl, quite inadvertently, becomes caught up in a major planned heist and is forced to fake credentials as a master swindler in order to stay alive. Like Cyberpunk, the show tackles anti-authoritarian themes among a diverse crew of outsiders. Stream Akudama Drive on Cunrchyroll or buy it from Prime Video.

Dexter Morgan is on the hunt for serial killers again in Dexter: Resurrection, and it looks like it could lead to some big trouble for him and Harrison very soon. The father and son had an unexpected reunion at the scene of the crime of the Five Borough Killer's latest murder, and Dex needs to be wearing those glasses all the time after what he missed.

The latest episode to hit the 2026 TV schedule didn't acknowledge it, but I immediately clocked why Harrison and Dexter's quick conference was more dangerous to their freedom than they may have realized. Take a look at the photo below, and that body cam right on Harrison's uniform on his right breast:

Dexter: Resurrection didn't mention the camera, or really draw attention to it in any way, but ensured it was in the frame for the entire conversation. In that conversation Dex said he had nothing to do with the killing, that he knew that Dan Stevens' FBK was responsible, and that he had linked up with Leon Prater's assistant Charley earlier that day.

I Have A Theory About Dexter: Resurrection And His Downfall. Why I Think Season 2 Could Address It

Should someone review that bodycam footage back at the station, I can imagine they're going to have some major questions for Harrison. At best, I'm sure his new co-worker/love interest Fiona will wonder why he let a witness to FBK leave the scene.

At worst, and what I imagine will be the most likely outcome, she will figure out Dexter is his dad and wonder why he was at the crime scene pursuing the FBK killer. Additionally, there will be questions about why he was pursuing the killer and why Harrison assumed he might be responsible for the crime.

If Dexter wasn't pursuing multiple high-profile serial killers at the same time, he might have had his eye on the ball. I have a feeling someone will eventually see this footage in the police department, and they'll have some questions for Harrison and Dexter.

There's also the slight possibility that the Dexter: Resurrection team missed this, though that feels unlikely. The fact that Harrison's body cam was so prominently on display in the scene, despite zero attention being drawn to it, has me convinced it'll come back up at a later date. #3522. Anne Hathaway's 2026 Sci-Fi Survival Movie Is Officially HBO Max's Biggest Streaming Hit

If you were disappointed by Anne Hathaway's dead-on-arrival Colleen Hoover movie "Verity," you might be interested in streaming one of her 2026 efforts that was actually good. HBO Max users certainly are. After a disappointing box office run, "The End of Oak Street," in which a suburban family is transported to dino-land, is finally getting the attention it deserves on the streamer.

"The End of Oak Street" trailers made it look like the the most fun dinosaur movie in years, and that turned out to be true. But the film is also surprisingly heartfelt, finding time between the dino fights and chase sequences to essentially explore the idea of home — the place where we're all supposed to feel safest — suddenly becoming the most unsafe place you could be. Writer/director David Robert Mitchell certainly delivers spectacle, but it's all in service of the characters and an interesting idea that powers the rest of the film.

Unfortunately, the box office returns for "The End of Oak Street" weren't quite what they could have been. The movie made $121.6 million in theaters on an $85 million budget, and if you know how the box office actually works, you're aware the film almost certainly didn't hit its break even point. Warner Bros. then rushed the movie to digital less than 30 days after it opened theatrically, and it remains unclear just how well it performed. But regardless of whether anyone made any money, the film is well worth a watch. Thankfully, HBO Max users now seem to be giving it the attention it always deserved.

"The End of Oak Street" is a thrilling dinosaur adventure that stars Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor as Denise and Greg Platt. The husband and wife live in a quiet Michigan suburb with their daughter Audrey (Maisy Stella) and son Brian (Christian Convery) circa 1982. Tensions lie beneath the surface of their seemingly idyllic life, though, with Denise feeling unfulfilled, Greg struggling to make ends meet, and the kids feeling like outsiders among their peers. Soon, however, they have bigger problems. One morning, the family wakes up to find their neighborhood has been transported back through time to a prehistoric age. Now, rather than social isolation and looming divorces, the biggest threats they face are of the scaly, sharp-toothed variety.

David Robert Mitchell previously oversaw one of the best horror movies of the 21st Century in "It Follows," but he's since proven he can deliver more traditional big-screen thrills with "The End of Oak Street." And while audiences didn't necessarily show up in droves at the multiplex, the film received positive reviews and earned an 86% "certified fresh" critical approval rating on Rotten Tomatoes. As it were, it appears that HBO Max users are as taken with Mitchell's family drama/dino adventure as most critics.

"The End of Oak Street" hit the streamer on November 13, 2026, and it subsequently shot to number one on the most-watched movies charts in multiple countries, including the United States (per FlixPatrol). At the time of writing, the movie occupies the top spot in 57 countries, and in several cases has been there since its debut. So, if you're yet to watch "The End of Oak Street," take this as a sign to rectify that immediately.

#3521. Nintendo Fans Blast New Switch 2 Release as ‘Paid Downgrade’

According to some fans, Dandori Academy gets a failing grade

So far, the Nintendo Switch 2 upgraded editions of games originally released on the Switch have been a bit of a mixed bag. While games like Kirby and the Forgotten Land received significant new content and noticeable performance upgrades, others such as Xenoblade Chronicles X weren’t quite as well received. According to many Pikmin fans, the recently released Switch 2 version of Pikmin 4 falls into the latter camp.

Pikmin 4: Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy is an upgrade for the 2023 Switch game with added levels and higher-resolution graphics. It came out last Thursday and costs $10 to upgrade from the original Nintendo Switch version. Unfortunately, the new version of Pikmin 4 currently has a dismal 1.9 out of 10 user score on Metacritic, a massive drop from the original version’s 8.9 user rating.

As for why it’s drawing so much ire, user reviews claim the Switch 2 version runs worse than it did on the previous system. Multiple players cite frame rate drops alongside longer load times. “This is essentially a paid downgrade and calling this a ‘lazy Switch 2 Edition’ or a ‘waste of money’ is an understatement for what is supposed to be an upgrade,” a Metacritic user review from PrestonandTom reads. They go on to claim that standard load times have gone from “six seconds to 30+ seconds” and that the frame rate has gone from a “consistent 30 FPS to an inconsistent 30 FPS.”

“Actively makes the game worse,” a review from Kevosan corroborates. “Longer load times than on NS1, frame drops, and glitches. The new content is NOT worth the trade-off. Standards are in the depths with this one.” Beyond the technical issues, some players also aren’t happy with the added Dandori Academy levels, which are apparently repetitive and reuse areas from the main story.

Still, there are a few upgrades that even the biggest detractors are fine with. The Switch 2 version of Pikmin 4 runs at a higher resolution, and some users commented that the voice support, which lets you give voice commands to the weird little dog-alien Oatchi, is a nice addition.

Many on the Pikmin subreddit weren’t quite as up in arms over the new version of Pikmin 4, with some saying that the negative reviews were being overdramatic. “0.6 is a score I’d only give to a game that is sub-functional,” one Redditor said about the review-bombed Metacritic page. Others argued that while the new Dandori Academy levels may reuse maps, the new enemy placements and other changes make these areas feel different.

Still, regardless of how fans feel about this upgrade, many Pikmin-heads are worried that the somewhat light changes compared to other Switch 2 editions mean that the series isn't being prioritized as highly as some of Nintendo's other tentpole releases. While Pikmin 5 hasn't been announced, at least the recently announced Pikmin shorts offer something to look forward to.

#3520. Five Smartwatch Heart Rate Zone Hacks Every Runner Should Know

If you've spent any time in or around running culture over the last few years, you've undoubtedly encountered someone preaching the gospel of Zone 2 cardio. Legend has it that easy, conversational effort cardio—also known as cardio that takes your heart rate into "Zone 2"—is the secret to unlocking everything from a bigger aerobic engine to faster race times and even a longer life.

To train by heart rate, you aim to keep your heart rate in the "zone" that gives you the desired workout. The catch is that Zone 2 is easy to get wrong, especially since no one can agree on what it actually means.  Your smartwatch can show you your heart rate, but many recreational runners will still drift into a “gray zone” that's too fast to be truly easy, and too slow to give them a real workout. If you're struggling to hit Zone 2 consistently, there are a few smartwatch hacks that can help.

Pace can be a distraction during easy runs, especially considering all the different variables that affect your effort, like hills, humidity, and general fatigue. A 9:30 mile might be Zone 2 on a flat, cool day and Zone 4 on a hot, hilly one.

Dig into your watch's activity settings (on Garmin, it's Activity > Data Screens; on Apple Watch, the Workout app's metrics layout; on Coros, Polar, and Suunto, similar menus) and put live heart rate zone front and center, ideally as a zone number or colored gauge rather than just a raw bpm figure (though this assumes these zones are accurate—more on that below).

Create an alert when your heart rate goes above or below a target range, delivered as a vibration pattern, a beep, or both. Set the alert for the upper boundary of Zone 2, and you've essentially hired a mini coach who taps you on the wrist whenever you get overzealous. Whenever you hear or feel that buzz, you’ll know you need to ease into a slower jog until your heart rate settles.

Instead of free-running and checking your numbers afterward, build structured workouts that carry the targets for you. In Garmin Connect, TrainingPeaks, Apple's Custom Workout feature, Coros Training Hub, or similar platforms, you can create sessions like "10-minute warm-up in Zone 1, 40 minutes in Zone 2, 5-minute cooldown" and sync them straight to your watch.

During the run, your watch displays the current step, the target range, and whether you're above, below, or in the pocket. Many will automatically advance between intervals and alert you when it's time to shift gears.

Heart rate-based intervals, like 4 x 4 minutes in Zone 4 with Zone 1 recovery, where you don't have to do mental math or check the clock.

Progressive long runs that start in Zone 2 and finish in Zone 3.

Hill repeats, where pace is meaningless but effort matters.

Most watches calculate default zones using a generic formula like 220 minus your age, which can be off by 10 to 20 beats for any given individual. If your zones are wrong, your Zone 2 training isn't Zone 2 training.

Here’s how to fix your watch’s heart rate zones:

Find your true max heart rate. The informal way is to just notice what number you see on your watch when you can no longer speak comfortably; the more formal way is this treadmill test. You can also look through your recent hard efforts, like races, hill repeats, or all-out intervals, and see the highest sustained heart rate you've recorded.

Use lactate threshold heart rate instead. Many watches can estimate this automatically after a few hard efforts, and zones built from threshold tend to be more personalized than ones built from max.

Customize the boundaries. Dive into the heart rate zone settings and input your own numbers. Some runners prefer the "MAF" method (180 minus age, with adjustments) for aerobic base building, and most watches let you set that as a custom range.

Recheck every few months. Fitness changes, and so do your zones.

A screen crowded with cadence, vertical oscillation, ground contact time, running power, and lap pace is a recipe for second-guessing.

Create a dedicated Zone 2 data screen with just two or three fields: current heart rate zone, elapsed time, and maybe distance. Turn off auto-scroll so it doesn't flip to a screen full of numbers you don't need. If your watch supports multiple activity profiles, make a separate "Easy Run" profile with this stripped-down layout and keep a different profile for tempo days and races.

A chest strap (or a forearm or upper-arm optical band) is generally more accurate and responsive than the wrist-based sensor on your watch. For heart rate training, where a few beats can mean the difference between Zone 2 and Zone 3, I recommend buying one. This COOSPO heart rate monitor is one of my favorites, and it's only $31.99.

The bottom line: Your smartwatch can make heart rate training far easier, but only if you set it up to support you rather than overwhelm you.

#3519. Zendaya “Felt Overwhelmed” on the Set of ‘The Odyssey.’ Luckily, Tom Holland Came to Support Her

On the set of The Odyssey, in which Zendaya plays the goddess Athena, there were some particularly challenging days, as the actor recalled during a recent special screening attended by the cast at Los Angeles’s Academy Museum of Motion Pictures. While filming certain scenes—especially those with a crowd of extras—the 30-year-old actor felt “incredibly nervous,” she said.

How did she manage to keep the situation under control? Thank her husband, Tom Holland, whom Zendaya says went to set that day to cheer her up. Spider-Man: Brand New Day star Holland also appears in The Odyssey as Telemachus, son of Odysseus and Penelope. And although he wasn’t scheduled to work at that particular moment, he showed up anyway to support his wife.

Matt Damon’s Odysseus consults with Zendaya’s Athena in The Odyssey.

“I felt overwhelmed, to say the least,” Zendaya said at the screening, as reported by the Daily Mail, with the actor looking stunning in her cream-colored one-shoulder dress, pixie cut, and Christian Louboutin stilettos. “It was interesting because I was on a night shoot, and I remember I came in and I was like, This is like, a pinch-me moment…. I’m in front of these people who I’ve admired, but I’m just like, I don’t want to mess this up.”

While she admitted that these emotions might have worked for her character, they were not so good for her state of mind: “I was incredibly nervous, which I guess is helpful for the scene, but there’s so many other background actors as well who are performing their hearts out—so many—stunt performers who are performing and giving the most beautiful performances.”

The turning point came when Holland stepped behind the scenes to encourage her. “It helped that Tom came to set that day, and he was, like, in the corner like, ‘You got this, you’re doing good.’” It was a team effort.

Zendaya and Holland are one of Hollywood’s most admired couples, not only for their discretion (they quietly married last August 4 in Surrey) but also for the care with which they address sensitive issues, such as mental health. Even in the cult series Euphoria, Zendaya’s character, Rue, grapples with psychological issues—in addition to addiction—as a way to raise public awareness and combat the stigma that often surrounds these kinds of situations.

Originally published in Vanity Fair Italia.

#3518. What Robert Pattinson's James Bond Casting Could Mean For His Batman Future

Is it just me, or is Hollywood shrinking these days? Skydance now owns Warner Bros. Discovery, which comes only a few years removed from Disney swallowing up 20th Century Fox in another corporate merger. Now, the same man has currently laid claim to two of the biggest names in the history of franchise filmmaking. And this is raising all sorts of questions about the fate of one of those names — a certain bat-eared superhero – in the near future.

Yes, today has brought us the martini-shaking news that Robert Pattinson has been officially chosen as our next James Bond. Not only does this mean that Pattinson now has three major IPs under his belt at the same time (including his upcoming role in "Dune: Part Three" later this year), but it also feels like our first major indication of Pattinson's future as Batman. As any Bat-fan can attest to, it hasn't been the easiest journey to bringing "The Batman II" from script to screen. The long-delayed sequel recently hit another setback when director Matt Reeves stepped away from filming, with Steven Soderbergh filling in for him. Making matters worse, the change in leadership for DC Studios following the merger between Warner Bros. Discovery and Skydance-Paramount has further thrown the state of Reeves' standalone films in disarray.

But perhaps this Bond announcement, of all things, could shine some light on Pattinson's role as Batman in the years ahead. Are his days in the cape and cowl numbered? Between some recent reporting and simply reading the tea leaves, we may have an idea of what this means for the future of Pattinson's "The Batman" movies.

Nothing in Hollywood occurs in a vacuum, as Robert Pattinson's James Bond casting throws into sharp relief. After all, who could've predicted the dizzying rise of the guy from "Twilight" becoming one of the industry's most recognizable and bank-breaking leading men of all? As it turns out, that principle also applies to the novelty of seeing the same man cast as both Bond and Batman at the same time — however short-lived that may be.

As fans paying close attention may have guessed, one development likely has much to do with the other. If we look back at the buzzy search for our new Bond over the last several months, it's clear that Pattinson's candidacy (along with Nicholas Hoult's) only cropped up in the eleventh hour. Industry insider Matt Belloni suggested as much in a recent Puck newsletter, handily explaining why most rumors failed to mention Pattinson's name in the early going. What's more, this timing also coincides with another bit of industry news: James Gunn and Peter Safran's ousting at DC Studios. With Matt Reeves' two biggest champions gone, might this uncertainty have a trickle-down effect? According to Belloni, it sure could:

"Even before director Matt Reeves was temporarily replaced by Steven Soderbergh due to a personal issue, Reeves had fallen far behind on ['The Batman Part II'], which eventually pushed the release date to February 2028. It's hard to believe that Skydance, and its new DC president, Jeremy Latcham, will go down that path again. Indulging a lengthy timeline on the company's number one franchise is probably not an option for the debt-laden Skydance. And without Reeves, Pattinson is unlikely to continue in the role, I'd guess."

Walk with me on this hypothetical, folks. After sitting out much of the initial frenzy surrounding the James Bond casting, Robert Pattinson finally got the call from Amazon and/or Bond director Denis Villeneuve following the shakeup at DC Studios. Previously, Pattinson and Matt Reeves may have been planning for at least one more film to cap off the "Batman" trilogy in the years ahead — and, to be clear, this could potentially still happen. But, without James Gunn calling the shots anymore, and with Skydance CEO David Ellison itching to get his own Batman franchise underway, Reeves saw the writing on the wall and gave Pattinson his blessing to pursue a different (yet more stable) franchise lead role.

That sure sounds plausible to us, even as we're simultaneously thrilled by this Bond casting and disappointed by the possibility that "The Batman Part II" could spell the end of Pattinson's time in Gotham. So goes the reality of art and commerce butting heads in this capitalist hellscape we've made for ourselves. If this truly is the end of the road for Pattinson and Reeves' "The Batman" franchise, well, that only makes us even more excited to see the sequel arrive in 2028. Meanwhile, the trade-off will be seeing Villeneuve and Pattinson reunite after "Dune: Part Three" for what may be the most highly-anticipated Bond movie since 2006's "Casino Royale."

That's not a bad consolation prize at all. Of course, all of this is merely informed speculation, and things could always change on a dime. Stay tuned to /Film for any and all updates in the weeks ahead.

Spoilers for the latest episode of Boston Blue, “Bloodlines” lie ahead.

Boston Blue Season 2 has been chugging right along amid the 2026 TV schedule, and viewers have been treated to some serious action and tense family drama. Mae Silver’s re-election (for Boston District Attorney) campaign, Sarah Silver’s impending marriage to Seth Yates and the reunion of Reagan brothers Danny and Jamie are among the highlights thus far. The season has also been eventful for Lena Silver and, based on the latest episode, I think she may end up in a messy storyline, which I’d prefer not to see.

Sonequa Martin-Green’s Lena Silver has a busy career, and she also has an eventful personal life, which has been tackled again this season. One of the biggest plot points revolves around her relationship with Detective Brian Rodgers (Ryan Broussard). At the tail end of Season 1’s finale, Rogers was in a car accident (which fans learned in Season 2 was part of an orchestrated hit). While Lena and Brian rehabbed together following the former’s own gun injury, Rogers became restless due to not being cleared to work again.

At the end of the episode, it was revealed that the flowers came not from Rogers but from Lena’s other ex-boyfriend, Dr. Troy Underwood, who was introduced in Season 1. It was established that prior to the events of the show, Troy and Lena dated, with the latter putting her life on hold to support him during medical school. That made it quite painful for Lena when Troy cheated on her during his training. Lena seemed to be done with the doctor but, amid this newest episode, she accepted a dinner invitation from him in order to hear him out.

So, with all of these plot threads in mind, my theory is that Lena and Troy will get closer and that Rogers will return to Boston after being assigned to a local DEA office. With that, Ms. Silver will find herself in the middle of a tense love triangle (and have to choose who she’ll want to bring to those Shabbat dinners). That’s the sense I’m getting, at least, but I’m hoping that’s not the case.

What It’ll Actually Take For Tom Selleck To Appear On The Blue Bloods Spinoff (Per Donnie Wahlberg)

First off, love triangles – whether they’re featured in procedurals or not – have become incredibly ubiquitous and feel somewhat clichéd at this point. Given that, I would hope that Boston Blue’s writers can think of something more interesting to do when it comes to handling Lena’s love life. There are also more specific reasons why this specific triangle would be relatively odd.

It would be weird for Lena to legitimately re-enter a relationship with Troy due to how he hurt her. Yes, Lena is a rational person who can extend grace but, given her characterization, it just feels weird for her to even think about getting back with someone who wronged her in such a deep way. Plus, if faced with a decision between Troy and Brian, I just can’t see her not choosing the latter, as her issue with Rogers amounts to a lovers quarrel. So, if Rogers comes back and is ready to accept help, why choose Troy?

Whatever the case, I’m getting the feeling that Lena’s romance journey will greatly differ from that of Danny and his partner, Maria Baez. Here’s hoping Silver gets a nuanced relationship story as Boston Blue’s second season continues. The show returns with a new episode on Friday, December 11 at 10 p.m. ET, and fans can stream it the next day with a Paramount+ subscription.

However, since it’s a fixed-view camera, keep in mind that you’ll need to position it carefully.

At these prices, the Ring Indoor Cam 2K is perfect for occasional live check-ins, while the Ring Battery Doorbell 2K is better suited to monitoring your front entrance. Buying both makes sense if you already have a Ring plan that covers extra devices.

#3515. Petition Demanding James Gunn And Peter Safran's DC Studios Return Passes 250K Signatures

It's true what they say: There really is nothing new under the sun. Whether it be 20, 200, 2000, or even two million years ago, humans have been behaving in surprisingly similar ways since we first figured out how to smash two rocks together and create fire. As easy as it is to believe that we're advanced and sophisticated and enlightened in all our modern sensibilities from our cave-dwelling ancestors ... well, maybe we're not so different after all, as the cliché goes.

Okay, I realize that's an unusually existential lede for an entertainment article this early in the week, but hopefully, you can see where we're going with this one. It felt like only an eyeblink ago when we were watching the #ReleaseTheSnyderCut fandom do their thing on social media in defense of Zack Snyder, the director formerly in charge of the direction of DC's movie and TV franchise. Now, his successor (and close friend) James Gunn is experiencing a similar sense of déjà vu in what has to be one of the most ironic developments in recent memory.

Only days after the news that Gunn and co-studio head Peter Safran were out at DC Studios, fans of Gunn's directorial work on 2025's "Superman" and his overall vision for the nascent DC Universe have banded together for a very familiar purpose. Yes, there's now another online movement hoping to get a major studio company to reverse course on a decision that goes up to the highest levels. A new Change.org petition titled "Keep James Gunn and Peter Safran as heads and co-presidents of DC Studios" has garnered quite a few signatures online — over 270,000, at the time of this writing.

At this rate, it's only a matter of time before somebody buys a billboard or flies a banner from a plane over Skydance HQ. While the DC Studios shakeup appeared to come as a shock to fans, it's fair to say many industry insiders figured that James Gunn's days at DC were numbered following the Warner Bros. Discovery/Skydance merger. Still, it's equally as true that neither Gunn nor Peter Safran really had much of a chance to get their rebooted universe off the ground in the first place. A solid "Superman" revival, a disastrous "Supergirl" movie, and a mid-budget "Clayface" origin story don't exactly provide a window into their plans as a whole (which reportedly spanned 10 years into the future).

Now, we'll simply have to wonder how things might have turned out in an alternate universe where the co-studio heads were allowed to cook uninterrupted.

....Unless, of course, David Ellison has his "Come to Jesus" moment as a result of some enthusiastic fans online. That raises the tantalizing question: Will this fairly sizeable petition have any effect on the wheels of machinery grinding away at Skydance? I hope any hopefuls among us are sitting down for this, because the answer is almost certainly not. But, hey, this sure beats toxic fans harassing and dogpiling and otherwise wreaking all sorts of mayhem on social media, right? (Actually, that's probably happening anyway, so scratch that.)

Even if absolutely nothing changes, the always-online Gunn can at least take some solace in knowing that many of us believe there was more to be explored with his vision of the DC Universe.

#3514. Glenn Close Gets Teary-Eyed as She Finally Gets Her Oscar at the Governors Awards

The day before the Governors Awards, a studio executive who had attended the past few years told me that she often found herself crying at the star-studded gala. The annual awards ceremony, held by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, is often an emotional event, with honorary Oscar statuettes bestowed on influential figures in the film industry. A tribute to Michael J. Fox in 2022 and a posthumous honor for Quincy Jones in 2024 left many guests misty-eyed.

At Sunday’s gala, that teary-eyed trend continued when Glenn Close finally got to hold her own Oscar, after eight nominations without a win. Others got emotional when Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, the independent producers from Killer Films, were honored for their tireless work making boundary-pushing and challenging movies. And when Floyd Norman, the 91-year-old artist who was the first Black animator to join Walt Disney Animation Studios, thanked his wife and five children, the crowd cheered along with him. Even though honoree Ridley Scott couldn’t attend, he dedicated his award to his late brother Tony Scott in a video message. “It is about time we all saw him with an Academy Award in his hand,” said Matt Damon in his remarks for Scott, who has been nominated for four Oscars but has never won competitively.

The presentation of honorary Oscars is often a way to correct Academy Award history, recognizing those who have been overlooked but deserve to be honored for their lifetime of dedication to storytelling and film. The Governors Awards ceremony is also a major stop on the Oscar season campaign trail, with a room packed full of stars and filmmakers from the year’s contenders.

This year that meant a surprising number of couple contenders, including Monica Barbaro and Andrew Garfield (who both star in Artificial), Carrie Coon and Tracy Letts (The Liberation), and Zendaya and Tom Holland. Though Zendaya and Holland arrived together and walked through the Ray Dolby Ballroom as a pair, they actually sat at different tables—Zendaya at the Dune table, with Timothée Chalamet and director Denis Villeneuve, and Holland at the Odyssey table, with director Christopher Nolan. Chalamet also made a date night out of the event, bringing Kylie Jenner with him.

The room held a mix of A-list Hollywood stars, like Tom Cruise (in support of Digger), Julianne Moore (The Debut), and Charlize Theron (The Odyssey), and breakout filmmakers of the year, like Obsession’s Curry Barker, La Bola Negra’s Los Javis, and Club Kid’s Jordan Firstman.

Another breakout of the season, La Bola Negra star Guitarricadelafuente, has been busy promoting the film as both an actor and a musician, having written the original song “La Nieve.” I wondered if he was exhausted from doing double duty. “I’m not tired,” he said with a smile, raving that he had enjoyed meeting many of the other songwriters in the race this year.

All four of the presenters who handed the Oscars to the honorees are also in the Oscar race this year. Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother star Mahershala Ali honored Norman; Wild Horse Nine star John Malkovich honored his Dangerous Liaisons costar Close; Julianne Moore, teaming up with Todd Haynes, honored Vachon and Koffler; and Damon, the star of The Odyssey, honored Scott.

As Close took the stage to accept the award from Malkovich, she wiped tears away from her eyes. The star of films including Fatal Attraction, 101 Dalmatians, The Wife, Albert Nobbs, and The Big Chill spoke about being raised in a religious cult and how, in her childhood, animated films were her only escape. She also spoke about being nominated for eight Oscars over her career, insisting that it didn’t phase her not to emerge victorious. “As an outsider, I have never worried about whether I was going to win or not,” she says. “I have always felt that the great honor is to be in the room.”

She wrapped up her speech with a strong statement against AI. “The craft of acting and of great storytelling has never been more vital to the existence of our fragile, violent, but capable-of-transcendence species,” she said. “We are not machines. We are flawed. Our imperfections are our salvation.”

Vachon and Koffler have been making indie films through Killer Films since 1995, championing movies like Far From Heaven, Boys Don’t Cry, Kids, Carol, and Still Alice (which won Moore her Academy Award for lead actress). They dedicated their awards to the many people they’d worked with over the years, some of whom were in the room. “We have walked into propellers with you and what has resulted is usually a piece of work that has touched somebody. Sometimes it’s seen by millions of people and sometimes it’s seen by tens of people,” said Vachon. “But our movies came to life and made it to the screen because writers and directors trusted us with their stories and actors knew we were creating an environment that enabled them to give their best performance.”

Many of the honorees spoke about the mentors and industry giants who had helped them along the way. Close said she’d promised her World According to Garp director, George Roy Hill, that she’d thank him if she ever won an Oscar. “I never got the chance to thank the man who put me in my first movie. Now I can,” she said, holding her statuette up high. Scott, the director whose prolific career output includes Thelma & Louise, Gladiator, Black Hawk Down, Alien, Blade Runner, and The Martian, told a story in his video message about making his brother star in his very first project, the 1965 short film Boy and Bicycle. “I’m flattered and proud to accept this award, but I also accept it for Tony,” Scott said of his brother, who died in 2012. “His great work would certainly have earned this recognition.”

#3513. Apple Won't Make a Small Phone so This Company Is Stepping In

Big smartphones have long been the norm. It seems many, if not most, of us prefer our smartphones to be akin to tiny tablets. Even Apple's smallest iPhone isn't that small, with a 6.1-inch display. (Compare that to the 5.4-inch iPhone mini it used to sell.) But just because a lot of us like it that way doesn't mean all of us do.

Despite what companies like Apple would lead you to believe, there are plenty of people out there who want their smartphones to be smaller. For some, the iPhone mini was perfect, featuring a design that most could use comfortably with one hand. While the sales might not have been steady enough for Apple to continue producing the mini line, anecdotally, I know quite a few people who would happily keep using iPhones this small, if only Apple would make more of them. Perhaps you know people like this too; maybe you're one of them.

While the rumor mill does not suggest that Apple plans to make a new iPhone mini, that doesn't mean the dream of the tiny smartphone is dead. Enter "Enough Phone," a new device with a humble goal: to create a "small, modern smartphone that's enough."

Enough Phone really does seem small. The company says its upcoming device is 133mm by 64mm, and less than 12mm thick. That's the equivalent of 5.24 inches by 2.52 inches, and less than 0.47 inches thick. It's remarkably similar to the iPhone 13 mini, at 5.18 by 2.53 inches, and 0.3 inches thick. While the Enough Phone might be a tad larger overall, and perhaps noticeably thicker, it's still reminiscent of that "mini" footprint.

The Enough Phone's 5.3-inch display isn't particularly modern, however. While we don't know the display type, we do know that it has a resolution of 1520 x 720, which may look less sharp to anyone coming from the 2340 x 1080 resolution of the iPhone 13 mini. I'd wager that most people interested in a device like this aren't looking for an ultra-sharp OLED display anyway, but it's worth noting here.

As for the Enough Phone's other specs, the company says it plans to pack in a 2.4GHz MediaTek Dimensity 7500 chip with 8GB of RAM, 128GB of built-in storage, though you can expand that with a microSD card (something you don't see on many smartphones these days). The current plan is to ship with a single 50MP Sony IMX766 rear camera, and a 32MP selfie cam, which would be amongst the highest-resolution front-facing cameras on any smartphone. It supports 5G, Wi-Fi 6, and eSIM, with the option to use a physical SIM as well.

Enough is also aiming to make its smartphone more repairable than the competition. While smartphone OEMs have made slight improvements to repairability in recent years, few phones are made to be opened up by the user, and their components replaced. While Enough Phone isn't fully modular, it is designed with easy-to-open screws, and comes with a fully replaceable 3,500 mAh battery. Combined with promised software support through 2032, Enough says this device "should last you into the next decade."

Now, all of these specs are targets, as the phone is currently in the prototype stage. Enough says that final details may change "slightly" during testing. I would at least hope that the dimensions, particularly the screen size, remain the same by launch. What will likely stay the same, however, are the ringtones: Enough says they hired composer Brian Squillance of LAANDS to produce the jingles for its phone, which is a neat touch.

Unfortunately for Apple fans, however, Enough Phone isn't an iPhone. That said, it doesn't have to be an Android phone, either. While you can buy the phone with Android 17 installed, you can also choose to run OdysseyOS, a minimalist "de-Googled" operating system made by SLEKE. Enough says OdysseyOS is meant for "intentional phone use," which might appeal to anyone looking for a phone that's "dumb" as well as small.

Of course, neither operating system is iOS. Unfortunately for Apple users, the only true iPhone options here are to continue using an old iPhone mini, which Apple does still support, or to opt for an iPhone 17e, the smallest iPhone the company currently makes. It's pretty easy to find a used and refurbished iPhone 13 mini for reasonable price; but while they can still run the latest version of iOS, you won't be able to take advantage of all of Apple's newest features. Plus, while there's no telling how long Apple plans to support the 13 line for, it won't support it forever—by iOS 28 or iOS 29, your phone might lose support entirely.

If the promise of a modern mini smartphone entices you, you can back the Enough Phone on Kickstarter today. While the company's $399 "Super Early Bird" reward is already sold out, as of this article, the "Early Bird" reward is still up. That reward costs $449, and includes a glass screen protector pre-installed, a protective case, a USB-C cable, a USB-C to 3.5mm headphone adapter, a hex screwdriver, and green "Founders' Edition" backplate screws. Enough says that the retail price for its phone will be $599 after the campaign, so you can save $150 by backing the phone today—if you're serious about small phones. The Enough Phone is slated for a May 2027 launch.
